x-tagGroups.name: Company Configuration
x-tagGroups.description: Company configuration objects and services are for creating and managing company-wide resources such as attachments, email templates, dimensions, and users.

x-tagGroups.name: General Ledger
x-tagGroups.description: The General Ledger is where a company creates and maintains accounts, journals, and financial reports. You use the General Ledger to post journal entries, design and run reports, create budgets, and more. Other Sage Intacct subscriptions automatically post transactions to the General Ledger in real-time.

x-tagGroups.name: Cash Management
x-tagGroups.description: Cash Management is used to manage your cash accounts, including banks, savings institutions, and charge cards—all in one centralized location.

Cash_Management_Bank transaction rule set run details

x-tagGroups.name: Accounts Payable
x-tagGroups.description: Accounts Payable (AP) enables you to keep track of your vendor accounts and bills. Basically, you enter and edit your vendor transactions, and then pay them.

x-tagGroups.name: Accounts Receivable
x-tagGroups.description: Accounts Receivable (AR) is used to manage a full AR cycle, including customers, receivables transactions, and generating reports.

x-tagGroups.name: Time
x-tagGroups.description: Time ensures that workers' time is recorded, workers are paid, and that overall project costs are tracked.

x-tagGroups.name: Expenses
x-tagGroups.description: Employees create and submit expense reports, consisting of individual line items, to receive reimbursement for approved out-of-pocket costs related to their jobs.

x-tagGroups.name: Purchasing
x-tagGroups.description: Purchasing is used to automate purchasing transactions and monitor and manage merchandise acquisition.
tags: Purchasing_Accounts Payable or direct GL account details

x-tagGroups.name: Order Entry
x-tagGroups.description: Order Entry involves the creation and management of customer orders. Activities related to order entry include managing data related to customer orders, processing order transactions, and running reports on customer orders.
tags: Order_Entry_Accounts Receivable or direct GL account details

x-tagGroups.name: Inventory Control
x-tagGroups.description: Use Inventory Control to track your merchandise and maintain and analyze your inventory. This subscription is fully integrated with the other Sage Intacct subscriptions, particularly Purchasing and Order Entry.

x-tagGroups.name: Project and Resource Management
x-tagGroups.description: Project and Resource Management enables services companies to automate many of the functions of financial project management.

x-tagGroups.name: Construction
x-tagGroups.description: Use Construction functionality to represent project work in a visual hierarchy (work breakdown structure), using the project, task, and cost type dimensions.

x-tagGroups.name: Contracts and Revenue Management

x-tagGroups.name: Tax
x-tagGroups.description: Sage Intacct provides support for determining, capturing, and reporting on sales tax, VAT, and GST.

x-tagGroups.name: Fixed Assets Management
x-tagGroups.description: Use Fixed Assets Management to help efficiently track, manage, and analyze your organization's fixed assets. Use it to streamline the entire fixed asset life cycle from acquisition to disposal.

x-tagGroups.name: Consolidation
x-tagGroups.description: Consolidation in Sage Intacct supports either multi-entity financial reporting or the aggregation of financial data from multiple entities into a single set of financial statements. This allows organizations to view their overall financial performance across all entities, while still maintaining separate books for each individual entity.

x-tagGroups.name: Reports
x-tagGroups.description: The Reports objects and services let you create, run, and monitor reports.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Account labels
tags.description:
Account labels provide descriptive names for General Ledger (GL) accounts used in Accounts Payable (AP) transactions and reporting. Note that account labels must be enabled in the AP application settings before they can be used.

**When to use:** Use to help identify correct GL accounts through intuitive naming. Account labels can also help control access, since users can code transactions using only those GL accounts that are assigned a label.

**Relationships:** Associated with a GL account and optional offset GL account.
Can include 1099 settings used when posting transactions with the label.

**Lifecycle context:** Created and maintained as reference data before transaction entry.
Selected on AP transactions to control account posting behavior and reporting classification.

For more information, see [About AP account labels](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_AP_account_labels) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Adjustments
tags.description:
Accounts payable adjustments represent vendor debit or credit memo transactions that increase or decrease the amount owed to a vendor. They help keep vendor balances accurate when corrections, credits, write-offs, or other adjustments are needed outside the standard bill process.

**When to use**: Use this object when an integration needs to create, retrieve, or manage adjustments to vendor balances without changing the original bill. It is useful for workflows that apply credits, record debit memos, correct payable amounts, or synchronize adjustment activity from another system.

**Relationships**: Each adjustment is associated with a vendor and can include adjustment lines that capture the individual transaction details. For VAT-enabled transactions, adjustment tax entries provide tax information for the related adjustment line.

**Lifecycle context**: This object participates in the payable adjustment workflow from draft or submission through posting and payment application. Its state reflects where the adjustment is in processing, such as draft, posted, partially paid, paid, reversed, or selected for payment.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Adjustment lines
tags.description:
Adjustment lines represent the individual line items within an AP adjustment, capturing the specific amounts, accounts, and details that make up the overall adjustment. They provide the transactional breakdown needed for accurate accounting, reporting, and tax handling.

**When to use**: Use this object when creating or retrieving the detailed components of an adjustment, such as distributing amounts across accounts, dimensions, or projects. It is essential when integrations need line-level accuracy for financial processing or reconciliation.

**Relationships**: Adjustment lines belong to a parent accounts payable adjustment and inherit key context such as the associated vendor and transaction header. They can also be linked to tax entries in VAT-enabled environments, which provide tax details tied to each line.

**Lifecycle context**: This object is used during the processing and posting stages of the adjustment workflow, where line-level details are defined, validated, and ultimately posted to the general ledger. It supports downstream reporting by preserving the granular breakdown of each adjustment.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Adjustment tax entries
tags.description:
For VAT enabled transactions, adjustment tax entries represent the tax details associated with an accounts payable adjustment. Tax entries capture how tax amounts are calculated, applied, and reported for the transaction. Tax entries ensure that adjustments reflect accurate tax treatment for compliance and financial reporting.

**When to use**: Use this object when creating or retrieving AP adjustments that include tax impacts, especially in regions or scenarios where tax must be explicitly calculated or itemized. It is also relevant when validating or auditing the tax breakdown applied to an adjustment. Create and maintain adjustment tax entries from the owning [AP adjustment line](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-payable/groups/adjustments/tags/accounts_payable_adjustment-lines) object.

**Relationships**: Tax entries belong to an owning accounts payable adjustment line and define the full financial and tax composition of the transaction. They rely on tax configuration objects such as tax solutions, tax codes, and jurisdictions to determine the correct tax treatment.

**Lifecycle context**: Tax entries are established during adjustment creation and calculation, and they are finalized when the adjustment is posted. They continue to play a role in downstream reporting, compliance, and audit processes.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Adjustment summaries
tags.description:
Summaries are collections of the same type of transactions, grouped together and posted to the General Ledger using the date determined by the summary frequency. Individual transactions in a summary are processed immediately.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving or reviewing grouped AP adjustments that should be
processed together. To create a summary for adjustments, use the [Accounts Payable summary](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-payable/tags/accounts_payable_summaries) endpoint.

**Relationships:** Can reference a parent summary and related bank account information,
and contains aggregate values such as total amount and posting details.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as grouped transaction batches that remain open while
adjustments are added, and are closed after processing is complete.

For more information, see [Accounts Payable summary overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=AP_summary_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Advances
tags.description:
An AP advance represents a prepayment made to a vendor before a bill is received, such
as a deposit or retainer fee.

**When to use:** Use when recording vendor prepayments, applying advance payments to
outstanding vendor bills, or retrieving advance payment activity for reconciliation.

**Relationships:** Contains advance lines that distribute the payment across GL accounts.
Associated with a vendor and linked to an AP summary. Optionally linked to a bank account
for reconciliation.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as a draft and submitted for payment processing. Once paid,
applied to future vendor bills to reduce outstanding AP balances. The advance state
transitions through workflow operations such as Submit and Reverse.

For more information, see [About AP advances](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Advances_with_Depts___Locs) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Advance lines
tags.description:
An advance line represents an individual line item within an AP advance, recording a
portion of the advance payment and its GL account distribution.

**When to use:** Use when creating advance lines to distribute an AP advance across GL
accounts, updating line amounts or dimensions, retrieving individual line details for
analysis or reconciliation, or deleting lines from an advance that is in a draft state.

**Relationships:** Owned by the AP advance object and linked to a GL account. Optionally
associated with an account label and dimension values such as department and location.

**Lifecycle context:** Created when an AP advance is submitted and retained as part of
the advance record for reporting and reconciliation.

For more information, see [About AP advances](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Advances_with_Depts___Locs) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Bills
tags.description:
Bills represent Accounts Payable transactions that record amounts owed to a vendor for goods or services. This object is the primary record used to track, manage, and settle amounts owed to vendors within the AP workflow.

**When to use**: Use this object when creating or managing vendor invoices in Sage Intacct, including importing bills from external systems or maintaining payable balances. It is commonly used in integrations that automate invoice ingestion or synchronize purchasing activity into Accounts Payable.

**Relationships**: Bills are associated with vendor records and include one or more bill lines that capture detailed charges, distributions, and tax information. They are also linked to downstream payment and adjustment objects that act on the payable after it is created.

**Lifecycle context**: Participates in the core processing stage of the procure-to-pay lifecycle, starting when a vendor charge is recorded and continuing through approval, payment, and posting. It acts as the central transaction that bridges purchasing activity and payment execution in Accounts Payable.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Bill lines
tags.description:
Bill lines are line items that represent charges for purchased items or services on a bill.
Use bill lines to record individual amounts, dimensions, and other details that roll up to the bill.

Bill lines represent the individual line items within a bill, capturing the detailed charges for goods or services, including amounts, accounts, and dimensional allocations. These records define how the total payable is distributed for accounting and reporting purposes.

**When to use**: Use this object when creating or updating detailed charges on a bill, such as specifying GL accounts, amounts, or dimensions for each expense line. It is commonly used in integrations that need to map itemized invoice data into accurate financial distributions.

**Relationships**: Bill lines are child records of a bill and inherit context such as vendor and transaction details from the parent. They are associated with GL accounts, dimensions, and tax entries, which provide the accounting and compliance details required for each charge.

**Lifecycle context**: Participates in the transaction processing stage by defining the detailed composition of a payable before approval and posting. These records directly influence how expenses are recognized in the general ledger once the bill is processed.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Bill tax entries
tags.description:
Bill tax entries represent the tax details associated with a bill line on VAT-enabled transactions, including calculated or specified tax amounts, rates, and applicable tax rules. These records ensure that taxes on vendor charges are accurately captured for compliance and financial reporting. Create and maintain bill tax entries from the owning [AP bill line](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-payable/groups/bills/tags/accounts_payable_bill-lines) object.

**When to use**: Use this object when your integration needs to apply, calculate, or override taxes on bill line items in VAT-enabled environments. It is commonly used when importing invoices that include tax breakdowns or when precise tax control is required.

**Relationships**: Bill tax entries are child records of bill lines and derive context from the parent bill and its associated vendor transaction. They also reference tax configuration objects such as tax details, which define the applicable tax type, rate, and posting behavior.

**Lifecycle context**: Participates in the transaction processing stage by defining tax amounts before the bill is approved and posted. These records directly impact how tax liabilities are calculated, recorded, and ultimately reported in the general ledger and tax filings.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Bill summaries
tags.description:
Summaries are collections of the same type of transactions, grouped together and posted to the General Ledger using the date determined by the summary frequency. Individual transactions in a summary are processed immediately.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving or reviewing grouped AP bill transactions and their posting context. To create a summary for bills, use the [Accounts Payable summary](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-payable/tags/accounts_payable_summaries) endpoint.

**Relationships:** Can reference a parent summary and related bank account information, and contains aggregate values such as total amount and posting details.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as grouped transaction batches that remain open while bills are added, and are closed after processing is complete.

For more information, see [Accounts Payable summary overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=AP_summary_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Amortization templates
tags.description:
An amortization template defines the default configuration for amortizing prepaid or deferred expenses across accounting periods, including how and when amounts are recognized. It ensures consistent and automated expense allocation from source transactions.

**When to use**: Use this object to manage the predefined amortization rules that should be applied when creating prepaid expense schedules from AP transactions or other sources. It is useful when your integration needs to standardize and automate expense recognition over time.

**Relationships**: Works with Accounts Payable transactions, such as bills, that supply the source amounts for amortization. It supports the creation of downstream prepaid expense schedules and entries that drive periodic journal postings.

**Lifecycle context**: Used during setup to define amortization behavior before transactions are processed. Its configuration drives the generation, scheduling, and posting of expense recognition entries over time.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Joint payees
tags.description:
A joint payee identifies an additional recipient, along with the vendor, for a joint check payment on an AP bill.

**When to use:** Construction subscription is needed. Use when a bill payment must be issued jointly to the vendor and another party, such as a subcontractor, so both names appear on the printed check.

**Relationships:** Owned by the AP bill and referenced when a payment that uses the joint check method is issued.

**Lifecycle context:** Added to a bill before payment and locked from further changes once referenced by a joint check payment, keeping the printed check details consistent with the completed payment.

For more information, see [Joint check basics](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Constr_JointCheck-basics) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Payments
tags.description:
An AP payment represents a payment transaction applied to one or more outstanding (AP) balances, such as vendor bills, credit adjustments, or advances. This object captures how payment amounts are allocated across specific AP documents, including support for partial payments, discounts, credits, and multi-document settlements.

**When to use**: Use this object when recording new vendor payments, retrieving payment activity, or reconciling outstanding AP balances as part of an automated or manual payment workflow.

**Relationships**: Linked to AP transactions such as bills, debit and credit adjustments, and advances, with line-level payment allocations.

**Lifecycle context**: Captures the payment stage of the AP lifecycle, reducing outstanding liabilities and completing the vendor payment process.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Payment lines
tags.description:
A payment line represents an individual line item within an AP payment. Each payment line records a portion of a payment, enabling detailed tracking of how payment amounts are structured and applied within a payment object.

**When to use**: Use to retrieve or analyze individual entries that make up a payment.

**Relationships**: Owned by the AP payment object and associated with payment details that link to underlying AP transactions.

**Lifecycle context**: Created during payment processing and retained as part of the final payment record for reporting and reconciliation.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Payment details
tags.description:
AP payment details represent how a payment is applied to specific accounts payable (AP) transactions, including bills, adjustments, and advances, with optional line-level detail.

**When to use**: Use to retrieve or validate how payment amounts are allocated across AP transactions.

**Relationships**: Owned by the AP payment object and linked to underlying AP transactions and their line items.

**Lifecycle context**: Created during payment processing to define allocation of payment amounts and retained for reconciliation and audit purposes.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Recurring bills
tags.description:
A recurring bill defines a schedule for automatically generating AP bills at regular
intervals, commonly used for fixed, repeating expenses such as monthly rent or service fees.

**When to use:** Use to automate AP bill creation for regularly-occurring, fixed-amount
expenses. Supports non-standard recurring transaction schedules and automatically creates
and posts bills based on the defined schedule.

**Relationships:** Linked to a vendor and optionally to a contract. Contains line items
that define the GL account and amount distribution. Associated with payment terms and a
recurring schedule that tracks execution history.

**Lifecycle context:** When a scheduled execution triggers, Sage Intacct automatically
creates and posts an AP bill. The generated bills can be viewed and managed independently
of the recurring bill.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Recurring bill lines
tags.description:
A recurring bill line represents an individual line item within a recurring bill,
defining the GL account, amount, and other transaction details for each charge.

**When to use:** Use to create, update, or retrieve charges on a recurring bill, such as GL account assignments, amounts, or dimension details for a specific line.

**Relationships:** Owned by the recurring bill. Associated with a GL account and
optionally linked to dimensions such as location, department, and project. May also
reference a transaction allocation template or AP account label.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as part of the recurring bill and used as the basis for
generating corresponding lines in each AP bill produced by the recurring bill schedule.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Recurring bill tax entries
tags.description:
A recurring bill tax entry records the individual tax details for a line on an AP recurring
bill. Tax entries are included on recurring bill lines for VAT-enabled transactions.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve tax entry details for lines on a recurring bill. To create
or update tax entries, create or update the recurring bill line that contains them.

**Relationships:** Owned by the recurring bill line. Associated with a purchasing tax detail
that defines the applicable tax type and rate.

**Lifecycle context:** Tax entries are generated as part of the recurring bill line and
provide the tax amounts used when the recurring bill produces AP bills.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Summaries
tags.description:
Summaries are collections of the same type of transactions, grouped together and posted to the General Ledger using the date determined by the summary frequency. Individual transactions in a summary are processed immediately.

**When to use:** Use when creating, retrieving, or reviewing grouped AP transactions that should be processed together.

**Relationships:** Can reference a parent summary and related bank account information, and contains aggregate values such as total amount and posting details.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as grouped transaction batches that remain open while transactions are added, and are closed after processing is complete.

For more information, see [Accounts Payable summary overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=AP_summary_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Terms
tags.description:
An AP term defines the credit period a vendor extends to your company, including when payment is due and any discounts or penalties that apply.

**When to use:** Use when creating a new payment term, retrieving or updating existing terms, or configuring due date calculations, early payment discounts, and late payment penalties that can be applied to vendor bills and other AP transactions.

**Relationships:** Associated with vendors and referenced by AP transactions, such as bills, to determine due dates and discount or penalty calculations.

**Lifecycle context:** Terms are configured before bills are created and applied when a bill is entered, driving the bill's due date and any discount or penalty calculations throughout the AP lifecycle.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Check runs
tags.description:
A check run processes up to 1,000 checks at a time in a single offline print job, grouping payment requests together under shared print settings such as check stock and checking account.

**When to use:** Use when creating a batch of checks to print, retrieving check run details or settings, or updating check run configuration such as check stock, checking account, or print options before the checks are printed.

**Relationships:** Referenced by AP payments that are added to the check run for batch printing, and associated with a checking account used to print the checks.

**Lifecycle context:** Created before payment requests are added, and its configuration controls how the included payments are formatted and printed together.

For more information, see [Check run overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Check_run_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendors
tags.description:
Vendors are individuals or companies that you pay for goods and services.

**When to use:** Use when adding a new supplier or service provider to the system before recording AP bills or purchasing transactions against them, or when retrieving or updating vendor payment settings, contact details, and account configurations.

**Relationships:** Linked to AP bills, payments, and purchasing transactions; bills and purchasing transactions are recorded against the vendor, and payments are applied to settle outstanding balances. A vendor can be associated with contacts (for pay-to, remittance, and 1099 recipient roles), AP terms (for payment due dates and discount rules), a vendor type (for reporting groupings), a parent vendor (to link a subsidiary to its owning entity), GL accounts (for expense and offset posting), price lists and price schedules (for default pricing on purchasing transactions), and payment providers and bank file setup records (for electronic payment delivery).

**Lifecycle context:** Vendors are configured before AP transactions are created. When vendor approval is enabled, a vendor must be in an approved state before AP bills and purchasing transactions can be posted.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor account numbers
tags.description:
A vendor account number is the account number that a vendor assigns to a specific entity location in a multi-entity company. For example, a telephone company might assign an account number to identify which entity is paying a bill.

**When to use:** Use to assign a vendor's account number to a specific entity location so that the number appears on payment documents for that entity, helping match payments with bills from the vendor.

**Relationships:** Owned by a vendor and linked to a specific entity location. Vendor account numbers are managed through the parent vendor's `vendorAccountNumberList` array.

**Lifecycle context:** Vendor account numbers are set up after a vendor is created and before payments are issued for that entity.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor bank file setups
tags.description:
Vendor bank file setup contains the bank account details required to deliver electronic payments to a vendor using a local bank file format.

**When to use:** Use to configure the bank account details for a vendor before generating bank file payment batches that pay that vendor electronically.

**Relationships:** Owned by a vendor. Vendor bank file setup records are referenced by bank file payment batches when generating payment files for the vendor.

**Lifecycle context:** Vendor bank file setup records are created before the first bank file payment batch is generated for the vendor. The bank account details are used when the payment batch is authorized and the bank file is submitted to the bank.

For more information, see [About bank files](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Bank_file_payment) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor contacts
tags.description:
A vendor contact associates a contact with a vendor, allowing multiple contacts to be linked to a single vendor under different category names such as main office or branch office.

**When to use:** Use to associate a contact with a vendor for organizing billing addresses, remittance information, or other location-specific contact details, or to retrieve the contacts linked to a vendor.

**Relationships:** Owned by a vendor. Each vendor contact links to a contact record in the company contact list.

**Lifecycle context:** Vendor contacts are set up after a vendor is created and before vendor-related transactions are processed. Contact details linked to a vendor are referenced in AP transactions and payment documents.

For more information, see [Vendor contact information](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Vendor_contact_information) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor email templates
tags.description:
A vendor email template links an email template to a vendor for a specific transaction type, automating standard messages sent to the vendor when that type of transaction document is issued.

**When to use:** Use to configure which email template is sent to a vendor for a specific transaction type, or to retrieve or update existing vendor email template configurations.

**Relationships:** Owned by a vendor. Each vendor email template references an email template from the company email template library and is associated with a specific transaction type.

**Lifecycle context:** Vendor email templates are configured before transaction documents are issued so that the automated messaging is in place when a qualifying transaction is created.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor payment providers
tags.description:
A vendor payment provider links a payment provider service to a vendor, enabling electronic payment delivery through that provider. Payment provider services, such as Vendor Payments powered by CSI, are available for US vendors accepting USD.

**When to use:** Use to enroll a vendor in a payment provider service or to retrieve and update the subscription status and preferred payment method for an existing enrollment.

**Relationships:** Owned by a vendor. Each vendor payment provider references a payment provider from the cash management module and can have an optional preferred payment method.

**Lifecycle context:** Vendor payment providers are created to initiate enrollment with the payment provider service. The `state` field reflects the subscription status as reported by the provider, progressing from `requestInitiated` through to `subscribed` or `canceled`.

For more information, see [Compare payment methods](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=HDI_Select_Payment_Method) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor restricted departments
tags.description:
A vendor restricted department limits a vendor to specific departments or department groups in a shared multi-entity company, preventing the vendor from being used outside those restrictions.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the department or department group restrictions configured for a vendor in a shared multi-entity company.

**Relationships:** Owned by a vendor. Each vendor restricted department references either a department or a department group. Vendor restricted departments are created and maintained through the parent vendor.

**Lifecycle context:** Vendor restricted departments are configured as part of vendor setup in a shared multi-entity environment. Once configured, they restrict which departments the vendor can be used with across the company's entities.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor restricted locations
tags.description:
A vendor restricted location limits a vendor to specific locations or location groups in a shared multi-entity company, preventing the vendor from being used outside those restrictions.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the location or location group restrictions configured for a vendor in a shared multi-entity company.

**Relationships:** Owned by a vendor. Each vendor restricted location references either a location or a location group. Vendor restricted locations are created and maintained through the parent vendor.

**Lifecycle context:** Vendor restricted locations are configured as part of vendor setup in a shared multi-entity environment. Once configured, they restrict which locations the vendor can be used with across the company's entities.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor types
tags.description:
Vendor types organize vendors into categories that are used for reporting. To share vendor
types across entities, create them at the top level. Creating vendor types in an entity
restricts them to that entity.

**When to use:** Use when categorizing vendors for reporting, assigning default 1099 form
settings to groups of vendors, or building a hierarchy of vendor types using parent-child
relationships.

**Relationships:** May have a parent vendor type to support hierarchical classification.
Referenced by vendor records that are assigned to the vendor type.

For more information, see [Vendor types](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_vendor_types) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor groups
tags.description:
A vendor group categorizes vendors for use in financial reports, allowing vendor data to appear as rows or columns.

**When to use:** Use to create or manage vendor groups that organize vendors for dimensional reporting. Set up vendor groups before building financial reports that use vendors as a dimension.

**Relationships:** Contains vendor members specified individually in `groupMembers` or selected dynamically using `memberFilter` criteria. When `isDimensionStructure` is `true`, the group can be added to the rows or columns of a financial report layout.

**Lifecycle context:** Vendor groups are set up before financial reports that use them are created. Once configured as a dimension structure, the group determines the row and column headings for vendor data in reports.

For more information, see [Vendor groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Vendor_dimension_groups_po) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Payable_Vendor totals
tags.description:
A vendor total provides a summary of the outstanding amount owed to a vendor, aggregated
across all AP transactions for that vendor.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving outstanding balances owed to a specific vendor or
across all vendors for reporting, reconciliation, or AP exposure monitoring.

**Relationships:** Associated with a vendor and optionally scoped to an entity. Reflects
the net balance from AP transactions such as bills, credit adjustments, and payments.

**Lifecycle context:** Represents the current AP balance position for a vendor. Updated
as AP transactions are created, paid, or adjusted throughout the AP lifecycle.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Account labels
tags.description:
Account labels provide descriptive names for accounts wherever the accounts are referenced in the product and in reports. Account labels are an optional Accounts Receivable feature.

**When to use:** Use when assigning descriptive names and related configuration to accounts used in Accounts Receivable transactions and reports.

**Relationships:** Associated with general ledger accounts, tax groups, revenue recognition templates, and deferred revenue accounts.

For more information, see [AR account labels](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_ar_account_labels) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Adjustments
tags.description:
An AR adjustment represents a credit or debit transaction that modifies the amount owed by a customer.

**When to use:** Use when recording, retrieving, updating, or deleting customer adjustments that change an outstanding balance.

**Relationships:** Associated with a customer, adjustment summary, adjustment lines, tax information, and related accounting dimensions.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as a draft transaction and may be posted, paid, or reversed as it moves through the Accounts Receivable lifecycle.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Adjustment lines
tags.description:
An adjustment line represents an individual debit or credit within an AR adjustment that modifies the amount owed by a customer.

**When to use:** Use when creating, retrieving, or updating the individual entries that make up an AR adjustment.

**Relationships:** Owned by an AR adjustment and associated with a GL account, dimensions, currency amounts, tax entries, and account labels.

**Lifecycle context:** Created and maintained as part of the owning AR adjustment throughout its Accounts Receivable lifecycle.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Adjustment tax entries
tags.description:
An adjustment tax entry provides tax information for an adjustment line in a VAT-enabled transaction.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving tax amounts and tax-detail information associated with an adjustment line.

**Relationships:** Owned by an adjustment line and associated with an order entry tax detail.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as part of adjustment-line tax processing and retained with the adjustment line for reporting.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Advances
tags.description:
An AR advance records a payment received from a customer before an invoice is created, such as a retainer.

**When to use:** Use when recording, retrieving, or updating customer payments received before invoicing.

**Relationships:** Associated with a customer, advance lines, payment information, reconciliation details, and related GL accounts.

**Lifecycle context:** Created before invoicing and applied or reconciled as the related customer transaction progresses.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Advance lines
tags.description:
An advance line represents an individual entry within an AR advance transaction.

**When to use:** Use when creating, retrieving, or updating the entries that make up an AR advance.

**Relationships:** Owned by an AR advance and associated with currency amounts, bank information, dimensions, GL accounts, and account labels.

**Lifecycle context:** Created and maintained as part of the owning advance throughout its Accounts Receivable lifecycle.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Bill back templates
tags.description:
A bill back template defines the GL accounts and department mapping used to automatically
generate an invoice and a corresponding bill when one entity provides goods or services to
another entity.

**When to use:** Use when setting up recurring inter-entity billing arrangements so that
qualifying transactions between entities are billed back automatically.

**Relationships:** Associated with an entity and containing one or more lines that map the
invoice GL account, bill GL account, and department used to generate the resulting bill back
transactions.

**Lifecycle context:** Configured once and then reused each time a qualifying inter-entity
transaction is recorded, automatically generating the corresponding invoice and bill.

For more information, see [Set up inter-entity bill back](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_bill_back) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Bill back template lines
tags.description:
A bill back template line defines the GL accounts and department used to generate an
individual invoice line and its corresponding bill line within a bill back template.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve, add, or maintain individual lines within a bill back
template, typically managed from the owning bill back template.

**Relationships:** Owned by the bill back template and references the invoice GL account,
bill GL account, and department used to generate the resulting bill back transactions.

**Lifecycle context:** Created when the bill back template is configured, and used whenever
the template runs to generate the resulting invoice and bill lines.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customers
tags.description:
A customer is any company to which you sell goods and services. Sage Intacct uses customer
information for record-keeping, printing names and addresses on forms such as invoices, and
determining the ship-to contact for tax calculations.

**When to use:** Use when creating customer records, retrieving customer account details,
updating contact or billing information, or managing credit limits and payment terms.

**Relationships:** Linked to AR transactions such as invoices and payments. Customers can have
a parent customer for hierarchical grouping. Associated with contacts, AR terms, price lists,
tax solutions, and GL accounts.

For more information, see [About customers](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_customers) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer contacts
tags.description:
A customer contact is a contact associated with a customer, used to store names, addresses,
and communication details for the people involved in customer transactions.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the contacts associated with a specific customer. Create
and manage customer contacts from the owning
[customer object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-receivable/groups/customers/tags/accounts_receivable_customers).

**Relationships:** Owned by the customer. Linked to a contact record in the company
configuration.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer email templates
tags.description:
A customer email template associates an email template with a customer to automate
standard messages for transactions such as invoices and statements.

**When to use:** Use to create, update, or retrieve email template associations for
specific customers.

**Relationships:** Owned by the customer. Linked to an email template in the company
configuration.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer item cross references
tags.description:
A customer item cross reference maps a customer's item identifier to the corresponding
item ID used in your company's catalog, making transaction entry easier and more accurate.

**When to use:** Use to create, update, or retrieve item identifier mappings for a specific
customer.

**Relationships:** Owned by the customer. Linked to an inventory item in the company
catalog.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer restricted departments
tags.description:
A customer restricted department limits which department or department group a customer
can be used with in a shared multi-entity company, preventing the customer from being
applied in the wrong entity.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the department restrictions applied to a specific
customer. Create and manage restricted departments from the owning
[customer object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-receivable/groups/customers/tags/accounts_receivable_customers).

**Relationships:** Owned by the customer. Linked to a department or department group
in the company configuration.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer restricted locations
tags.description:
A customer restricted location limits which location or location group a customer can
be used with in a shared multi-entity company, preventing the customer from being
applied in the wrong entity.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the location restrictions applied to a specific
customer. Create and manage restricted locations from the owning
[customer object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-receivable/groups/customers/tags/accounts_receivable_customers).

**Relationships:** Owned by the customer. Linked to a location or location group in
the company configuration.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer messages
tags.description:
A customer message is a predefined text message that can be associated with a customer record and displayed on related invoices.

**When to use:** Use when creating reusable message templates to display on invoices generated for a specific customer.

**Relationships:** Linked to a customer using the `customerMessage` property on the customer record. When a customer with an associated message is invoiced, the message text is applied to the customer message field on the invoice.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer types
tags.description:
A customer type is a category used to classify customers into groups such as resellers and end users.

**When to use:** Use when classifying customers by type to support filtering, reporting, and management of customer information.

**Relationships:** Linked to customer records assigned the type. Customer types support a parent-child hierarchy for nested categorization.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer totals
tags.description:
A customer total provides a read-only summary of the total amount due from a customer.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving the outstanding balance owed by a specific customer, for example to support reporting or collections workflows.

**Relationships:** Linked to a customer record and optionally to an entity location.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer electronic payments
tags.description:
A customer electronic payment represents a payment made by a customer online using a credit card or ACH wire transfer, processed through PayPal or Authorize.Net.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving electronic payment records to review transaction details, payment state, or reconciliation status.

**Relationships:** Linked to an AR payment and a customer record.

**Lifecycle context:** Captures the result of an electronic payment transaction submitted through an online payment processor, including the payment method, processing result, and bank reconciliation details.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer groups
tags.description:
A customer group categorizes customers into named groupings for the purpose of structuring financial reporting.

**When to use:** Use when creating or managing groups of customers to apply to report dimensions, filter sets, or specific member lists.

**Relationships:** Contains customer records as members, either as a specific list defined in the `groupMembers` array or as a dynamically filtered set defined by `memberFilter` criteria.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Delivery histories
tags.description:
A delivery history record tracks each time an invoice or other transaction was delivered to a customer by print, email, or online delivery.

**When to use:** Use to review or audit when and how a specific transaction was delivered
to a customer.

**Relationships:** Linked to the delivered transaction and to any supporting document
attachment included with the delivery.

**Lifecycle context:** Created automatically each time a transaction is printed, emailed,
or delivered online, providing a read-only audit trail of delivery activity.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Invoices
tags.description:
An AR invoice represents an invoice sent to a customer requesting payment for goods or services provided.

**When to use:** Use when creating customer invoices, retrieving invoice details, updating invoice information, or managing invoice lifecycle states as part of AR billing workflows.

**Relationships:** Linked to a customer and associated payment terms. Contains one or more invoice lines, each with a GL account assignment. Invoices can be grouped into invoice summaries for batch GL posting.

**Lifecycle context:** An invoice starts in `draft` state and transitions to `posted` when submitted. It moves to `partiallyPaid` or `paid` as payments are applied, and can be `reversed` if voided.

For more information, see [About managing invoices - Accounts Receivable](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Viewing_and_Managing_Invoices) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Invoice lines
tags.description:
An invoice line represents an individual line item within an AR invoice, recording the GL account assignment, amount, and dimension details.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve, add, or update individual line items on an AR invoice. Line items can also be managed directly through the invoice.

**Relationships:** Owned by the AR invoice. Each line is associated with a GL account and can reference an account label, allocation template, and dimensions such as location, department, project, customer, and item. A line can also have associated tax entries.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as part of an invoice and retained as part of the final invoice record for payment tracking, reporting, and reconciliation.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Invoice tax entries
tags.description:
An invoice tax entry provides the VAT tax details for an AR invoice line item.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve tax entries associated with an AR invoice line. Tax entries are created automatically for VAT-enabled transactions and can also be managed directly through the invoice line.

**Relationships:** Owned by the AR invoice line. Each tax entry is linked to an Order Entry tax detail that defines the applicable tax rules.

**Lifecycle context:** Created automatically when a VAT-enabled invoice line is processed and retained as part of the invoice record.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Invoice summaries
tags.description:
An AR invoice summary is a collection of AR invoices grouped together for batch GL posting and processing.

**When to use:** Use when creating invoice batches, retrieving summary details, or checking whether a summary is open for new invoices to be added.

**Relationships:** Contains AR invoices of the same record type. A summary can be linked to a parent summary for hierarchical grouping. The GL posting date on the summary controls when included invoices post to the general ledger.

**Lifecycle context:** A summary starts as `open`, allowing invoices to be added. Once `closed`, no further invoices can be added. When posted, the included invoices are recorded in the general ledger.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Payments
tags.description:
A payment represents a payment transaction received from a customer and applied to one or more outstanding AR balances, such as invoices, debit memos, or adjustments.

**When to use:** Use when recording customer payments, applying payments to open invoices, or reconciling payment activity in Accounts Receivable.

**Relationships:** Linked to customer records, payment summaries, payment details, and payment line items that allocate the payment across invoice or adjustment balances.

**Lifecycle context:** Created during the payment collection workflow, then posted and reconciled as the payment is applied and settled.

For more information, see [Payments from customers](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_ar_payments) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Payment details
tags.description:
A payment detail represents a single allocation within a payment, identifying the invoice, adjustment, advance, or line item that the payment applies to and the amount received.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving the specific transaction or line-level allocation tied to a payment, such as the invoice and amount applied to a payment record.

**Relationships:** Owned by the AR payment and linked to invoice, adjustment, advance, and payment line records that define how the payment is allocated.

**Lifecycle context:** Created during payment processing and retained as part of the payment record for reconciliation, reporting, and audit review.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Payment lines
tags.description:
A payment line represents an individual allocation within an AR payment, recording how a payment is applied to an invoice, adjustment, or other AR balance.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving or reviewing the specific line-level allocations that make up a customer payment.

**Relationships:** Owned by the AR payment and linked to the invoice, adjustment, or related records that define how the payment is distributed.

**Lifecycle context:** Created during payment processing and retained as part of the final payment record for reconciliation and reporting.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Payment summaries
tags.description:
A payment summary groups customer payment transactions for processing and posting, helping track the payments that are being reviewed, posted, or reconciled together.

**When to use:** Use when grouping customer receipts for posting, tracking open payment batches, or reviewing payment activity in Accounts Receivable.

**Relationships:** Associated with payment records, bank accounts, undeposited funds accounts, and summary state settings that control how payment batches are processed.

**Lifecycle context:** Created during the payment collection workflow, then kept open or closed as transactions are posted and reconciled.

For more information, see [Payment Summaries overview - Accounts Receivable](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=AR_payment_summaries_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Recurring invoices
tags.description:
A recurring invoice represents an AR invoice that is generated automatically at fixed intervals based on a recurrence schedule you define.

**When to use:** Use when setting up automated billing for subscriptions, retainers, or other charges that repeat on a fixed schedule, or when retrieving and updating existing recurring invoice schedules.

**Relationships:** Linked to a customer, payment terms, and one or more GL accounts through its lines. Each occurrence generates a new AR invoice based on the schedule and scheduled operation associated with the recurring invoice.

**Lifecycle context:** Drives the recurring billing lifecycle by automatically creating new invoices at each scheduled interval until the recurrence ends or is canceled.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Recurring invoice lines
tags.description:
A recurring invoice line represents an individual line item within a recurring invoice, recording the amount, GL account, and dimensions applied for each occurrence.

**When to use:** Use to create, retrieve, or maintain the individual charges that make up a recurring invoice.

**Relationships:** Owned by the recurring invoice and associated with a GL account, account label, and other dimensions such as location, department, or project.

**Lifecycle context:** Created when the recurring invoice is set up, either along with the invoice or added afterward, and used as the template for line-level charges generated with each scheduled invoice occurrence.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Recurring invoice tax entries
tags.description:
A recurring invoice tax entry represents tax details captured for a recurring invoice line when VAT is enabled.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve tax information calculated for a recurring invoice line, such as the tax rate and tax amount applied.

**Relationships:** Owned by the recurring invoice line and associated with an order entry tax detail.

**Lifecycle context:** Generated automatically when a recurring invoice line is created for a VAT-enabled transaction.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Revenue recognition templates
tags.description:
A revenue recognition template defines how to amortize deferred revenue for an Accounts Receivable label or Order Entry Item GL group.

**When to use:** Use when setting up automated revenue recognition schedules for deferred revenue transactions.

**Relationships:** Associated with an account label or an item GL group, and used to generate revenue recognition schedules for transactions that reference the template.

**Lifecycle context:** Defines the recognition method, schedule, and posting behavior applied when revenue recognition schedules are generated and posted.

For more information, see [Revenue recognition templates - AR or Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Defining_Revenue_Recognition_Templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Summaries
tags.description:
An AR summary is a collection of the same type of transactions, grouped together for processing. A summary can be open or closed.

**When to use:** Use to group invoices, adjustments, and deposits for processing, to control when they post to the general ledger, or to open and close a group of transactions.

**Relationships:** Contains AR transactions such as invoices, adjustments, and deposits. A summary can have a parent summary.

**Lifecycle context:** Invoices, adjustments, and deposits can be added to a summary while it is open.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Terms
tags.description:
An AR term represents the rules a company establishes for extending credit to customers,
including due dates, early payment discounts, and late payment penalties.

**When to use:** Use when setting up payment terms that can be applied to AR transactions
and customer records.

**Relationships:** Associated with AR transactions and customers that reference the term
for due date and discount calculations.

**Lifecycle context:** Set up during company configuration and then referenced by AR
transactions and customer records whenever due dates, discounts, or penalties need to be
calculated.

For more information, see [AR terms](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_ar_terms) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Territories
tags.description:
A territory represents a geographic or organizational area optionally assigned to
customer records and used for categorizing and reporting on Accounts Receivable data.

**When to use:** Use when filtering or categorizing transactions and reports by region,
especially for companies with multiple territories.

**Relationships:** Can be assigned to customer records and organized into a parent-child
hierarchy of territories.

**Lifecycle context:** Set up during company configuration and then assigned to customer
records for use in filtering and categorizing AR reports.

For more information, see [Territories](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Territory_Information) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Territory groups
tags.description:
A territory group represents a named collection of territories, used to simplify
reporting and categorization across a related set of territories.

**When to use:** Use when you need to generate reports that contain data for a
particular set of territories as a single group.

**Relationships:** Contains one or more territories as members, each with a defined
sort order within the group.

**Lifecycle context:** Set up during company configuration and then used whenever
reports need to be generated for the territories in the group.

For more information, see [Territory groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Territory_Group_Information) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Shipping methods
tags.description:
A shipping method represents the specific way goods are transported to a customer,
such as UPS, FedEx, or hand delivery.

**When to use:** Use when setting up or retrieving the shipping options available for
Order Entry transactions.

**Relationships:** Referenced by Order Entry transactions to calculate the ship-by date
based on the estimated days in transit.

**Lifecycle context:** Set up during company configuration and then selected on Order
Entry transactions whenever the ship-by date needs to be calculated.

For more information, see [Shipping methods](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_shipping_methods) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Manual deposits
tags.description:
A manual deposit represents a deposit transaction used to record money received that
isn't related to an invoice, such as an over-the-counter cash sale.

**When to use:** Use when recording miscellaneous cash receipts that aren't tied to an
invoice, or when reconciling deposits against a bank account.

**Relationships:** Linked to the customer and bank account associated with the deposit,
and optionally grouped into a manual deposit summary, with one or more deposit lines
recording GL account and amount details.

**Lifecycle context:** Represents a completed cash receipt recorded directly against a
bank account, outside the standard invoice-to-cash workflow.

For more information, see [AR manual deposits](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_ar_deposits) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Manual deposit lines
tags.description:
A manual deposit line represents an individual line item within a manual deposit,
recording the GL account, amount, and dimension details for a portion of the deposit.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the individual entries that make up a manual deposit.
Create lines through the `lines` collection on the owning
[manual deposit object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-receivable/tags/accounts_receivable_manual-deposits).

**Relationships:** Owned by the manual deposit and associated with a GL account, account
label, currency amounts, and dimensions such as location and department.

**Lifecycle context:** Created and maintained as part of the owning manual deposit
throughout its Accounts Receivable lifecycle.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Manual deposit summaries
tags.description:
A manual deposit summary groups payments received from customers, such as quick or
manual deposit payments, for processing and posting.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving or reviewing manual deposit summaries, such as
checking whether a summary is open or closed, reviewing its GL posting date, or seeing
the total amount of deposits grouped within it. To add a manual deposit to a summary,
use the [manual deposit object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/accounts-receivable/tags/accounts_receivable_manual-deposits) endpoint.

**Relationships:** Associated with manual deposits and optionally linked to a parent
summary for hierarchical grouping. The GL posting date on the summary controls when
included deposits post to the general ledger.

**Lifecycle context:** A summary starts as `open`, allowing manual deposits to be added.
Once `closed`, no further deposits can be added.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Dunning levels
tags.description:
A dunning level defines the overdue-invoice criteria and notice settings used to determine
when and how a dunning notice is sent to a customer.

**When to use:** Use when configuring the escalation tiers of the dunning process, such as
the days overdue or amount thresholds that trigger a particular notice.

**Relationships:** Associated with the print template, email template, and numbering sequence
used to generate notices, and referenced by dunning notices that apply the level.

**Lifecycle context:** Configured before the dunning process runs, defining the escalation
tier that a dunning notice uses once an invoice meets the level's overdue criteria.

For more information, see [Add dunning levels](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Add_dunning_levels) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Dunning customers
tags.description:
A dunning customer represents a customer included in a dunning notice, along with the
overdue invoices, delivery method, and notice details generated for that customer.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the customers and overdue invoice details included in a dunning notice.

**Relationships:** Owned by the dunning notice and created automatically when the notice is
generated; includes references to the customer, dunning level, email template, and invoices
included in the notice. Dunning customers cannot be created or updated directly.

**Lifecycle context:** Captures the customer-level detail generated during the dunning notice
process, including the invoices and delivery method used to notify the customer.

For more information, see [Dunning notices](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_dunning_notices) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Dunning invoices
tags.description:
A dunning invoice is an overdue invoice included in a dunning notice sent to a customer.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the overdue invoices included for a customer as part of a dunning notice.

**Relationships:** Owned by the dunning customer and created automatically when a dunning notice is generated; dunning invoices cannot be created or updated directly.

**Lifecycle context:** Captures the invoice-level detail generated during the dunning notice process, recording which overdue invoices were included for a customer at the time the notice was sent.

For more information, see [Dunning notices](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_dunning_notices) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Dunning notices
tags.description:
A dunning notice is a notification sent to customers who have overdue invoices, generated
as part of the dunning process used to communicate with customers and collect overdue balances.

**When to use:** Use when generating, reviewing, or sending notices to customers with
overdue invoices as part of a collections workflow.

**Relationships:** Linked to a dunning level that defines the escalation criteria and
templates used, and owns the dunning customers and associated invoices included in the notice.

**Lifecycle context:** Represents the communication step in the dunning process, notifying
customers of overdue balances before further collection action is taken.

For more information, see [Dunning notices](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_dunning_notices) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer refunds
tags.description:
A customer refund returns money to a customer, such as when the customer has a negative balance, an unused advance, or an unused credit.

**When to use:** Use to issue a refund when another invoice will not be created for the customer or when the customer would like their money back.

**Relationships:** Associated with a customer and a financial account. Contains refund lines and refund details that link to the underlying AR transactions, such as negative invoices, advances, and overpayments. Belongs to an AR summary.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer refund lines
tags.description:
A customer refund line represents an individual entry in a customer refund, recording the amount refunded for a GL account.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve or analyze the individual entries that make up a customer refund.

**Relationships:** Owned by the customer refund and associated with a GL account and dimensions such as location and customer.

tags.name: Accounts_Receivable_Customer refund details
tags.description:
A customer refund detail records how much of a customer refund applies to an advance, adjustment, negative invoice, or overpayment, and includes other details about the refund, such as its state.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the individual transactions that make up a customer refund.

**Relationships:** Owned by the customer refund and linked to the refund line and to the underlying AR transaction being refunded.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Financial institutions
tags.description: A financial institution serves as an umbrella object for bank accounts that use the same sign-in process to connect to bank feeds.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank accounts
tags.description: This object provides information about a bank account, which can be a checking, savings, or a credit card account.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Checking accounts
tags.description:
A checking account represents a specific type of cash account used to manage day-to-day transactions, such as vendor payments, customer deposits, payroll and reconciliations.

For more information, read about [checking accounts](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_set_up_checking_accounts) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Credit card accounts
tags.description:
Sage Intacct defines credit card accounts as including both credit cards and debit cards. In Accounts Payable, there's a difference between the two.

* A credit card is a cash account that's related to a credit card vendor. The credit card account in Sage Intacct represents the actual credit card in the real world. Record charges made on this card in the Cash Management application.

* A debit card is associated with a checking account and is another way to debit that account. When a debit card charge is recorded, the bank account is debited and the transaction is final.

Although treated differently in Accounts Payable, credit and debit cards are treated the same way in Accounts Receivable. A customer payment made with either type of credit card debits that customer account and deposits the payment into your account.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Savings accounts
tags.description: Provides the relevant information for a savings account, including account ID, number, and so on.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transactions
tags.description:
Bank transactions represent individual bank account or credit card transactions recorded in a bank feed. They can be matched to existing transactions in Sage Intacct or created as new transactions for reconciliation.

For more information, read about [bank transactions](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_bank_transactions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction rule sets
tags.description:
Bank transaction rule sets act as containers for matching and creating rules. The rules determine how to match incoming bank transactions or create new transactions for reconciliation in Sage Intacct.

For more information, read about [bank transaction rule set run details](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_rules_rule_sets) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction rule set run logs
tags.x-displayName: Bank transaction rule set run logs
tags.description:
Bank transaction rule set run logs are used to view how well a rule set, or the match and create rules within it, are performing. They provide detailed information about each execution of a bank transaction rule set, including the number of transactions processed, matched, and created, as well as any errors encountered during the run.

For more information, read about [bank transaction rule set run logs](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_rules_rule_sets) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction rule set run details
tags.x-displayName: Bank transaction rule set run details
tags.description:
Bank transaction rule set run details records contain information about the execution of individual rules within a bank transaction rule set during a specific run. They are part of a bank transaction rule set run log which provides an overview of the execution of a bank transaction rule set against bank transactions.

For more information, read about [bank transaction rule set run details](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_rules_rule_sets) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction rules
tags.description: Bank transaction rules determine whether incoming bank transactions are matched to existing Sage Intacct transactions or used to create new transactions. A `match` rule matches incoming bank transactions to existing Sage Intacct transactions. A `create` rule uses incoming bank transactions to create new Sage Intacct transactions.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction rule filters
tags.description: Filters define which transactions a bank transaction rule considers when attempting to find a match. You can filter by Intacct transactions or bank transactions. For `match` rules, filters are optional. For `create` rules, a filter must be based on bank transaction posting dates. `Create` rules can only filter by bank transactions.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction rule groups
tags.description: Grouping (optional) organizes transactions within a bank transaction rule. A rule first applies any defined filters. After filtering, the rule attempts to create a group. A rule can group either bank transactions or Intacct transactions. For `match` rules, only Intacct transactions can be grouped.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction rule maps
tags.description: A bank transaction rule map links a bank transaction rule to a rule set.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction rule matches
tags.description: Bank transaction rule matches, used within bank transaction rules, determine how incoming bank transactions are automatically matched to existing Intacct transactions. Incoming transactions may originate from a bank feed or an import file.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction assignment rules
tags.description:
Bank transaction assignment rules automatically assign a customer to an unmatched bank deposit transaction in a checking or savings account based on pre-defined criteria. Assignment rules run for incoming and existing unmatched bank transaction credits so payment type transactions are assigned to a customer.

For more information, read about [bank transaction assignment rules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_assignment_rules) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank transaction assignment rule filters
tags.description:
Bank transaction assignment rule filters are used in bank transaction assignment rules. They define criteria for automatically assigning customers to unmatched bank deposit transactions based on specific attributes such as transaction type, amount, or description. Assignment rules run for incoming and existing unmatched bank transaction credits so payment type transactions are assigned to a customer. 

For more information, read about [bank transaction assignment rules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_assignment_rules) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank fees
tags.description:
Bank fees are financial transactions that capture charges or incentives incurred in connection with bank account activity.

For more information, read [about bank interest and charges](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_bank_interest) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank fee lines
tags.description: Bank fee lines represent interest and bank charges assoicated with a bank fee. Create and maintain bank fee lines from the owning bank fee.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank fee tax entries
tags.description:
Bank fee tax entries contain tax entry details for VAT enabled bank fee lines. Create and maintain bank fee tax entries from the owning bank fee line.

For more information, read about [entering taxable transactions](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Enter_taxable_transactions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank files
tags.description:
Bank files are generated files that contain payment information for electronic payments. Sage Intacct supports bank files in a local bank file format that can be uploaded to the company's banking portal to provide the bank with the required payment data. The bank can then process payments using the bank file. 

For more information, read about [bank files](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Bank_file_payment) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank file details
tags.description:
Bank file details are associated with a bank file and provide detailed information about a bank file payment transaction, such as payment details and bank file errors.

For more information, read about [bank files](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Bank_file_payment) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank feeds
tags.description:
A bank feed is a connection between Sage Intacct and your bank. Sage Intacct receives transactions from the bank and automatically matches them using reconciliation rules during the month-end close. Bank feeds allow you to access transaction records for bank reconciliations directly using Sage Cloud Services, or you can provide your own transaction records as XML elements.

Bank feeds are currently supported for checking account reconciliation. When you create a bank feed, the bank transactions become available for matching against existing transactions during reconciliation.

For more information, read [an overview of bank feeds](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Bank_rec_bank_feeds) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank reconciliations
tags.description:
Bank account reconciliation is where you can match bank transactions throughout the month or even perform daily or "soft" reconciliations to help eliminate your month-end close. There are three ways to reconcile an account in Sage Intacct, manually, by importing a bank file, or by connecting to a bank feed.

For more information, read about [bank reconciliation](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Bank_rec_converting_over) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Bank reconciliation records
tags.description:
A bank reconciliation record contains detailed information about a single bank transaction. It is either manually added from the owning bank reconciliation object or imported from a file or bank feed. During the reconciliation process, the bank reconciliation record is matched to a transaction previously posted in the General Ledger (GL). Bank reconciliation records are created and updated in the owning bank reconciliation object.

For more information, read [about reconciliation](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_reconciliations) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Cash_Management_Account reconciliation source records
tags.description:
An account reconciliation source record represents a single imported external transaction, such as a bank or credit card entry. It is used to match against posted transactions during the reconciliation process.
