tags.description: A personal estimation of how complete a cost type is as of a specific date. It is used to track percent completion values and dates by entering "as of dates" and percentages as the cost type progresses.

tags.name: Construction_Project contract billing invoice details
tags.description: Project contract billing invoice details hold billing details for a single project contract line.

tags.name: Construction_Project contract billing invoice summaries
tags.description: Project contract billing invoice summaries enable a construction company to properly report on project contract billing totals, and are instrumental in creating industry-standard invoice templates. The fields in these objects contain the detail of the contract value, the amount that has been billed, is left to bill and the retainage held and billed during the contract duration.

tags.name: Construction_Rate tables
tags.description:
A construction rate table provides markup and pricing information to be used for generating project generated invoices. Every rate table contains lines for each transaction type which identify the criteria to use when applying markup and pricing for that transaction type. The transaction types include timesheets, purchase orders, accounts payable, general ledger, credit cards, and employee expenses.

For more information, read about [setting up](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_rate_tables) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_Rate table accounts payable lines
tags.description:
Construction rate table accounts payable lines contain criteria for applying a default markup percentage to matching accounts payable transactions during invoicing. They are owned objects of a rate table object. You create, update, and delete accounts payable line objects through operations on the owning rate table.

* Each line requires only 1 value be provided. 
* Lines with the exact same values (excluding description and markup %) are considered duplicates and are not allowed. 
* If no value is given for a property then the line matches on any transaction, otherwise it only matches on transactions with that property. 
* Lines with the most matches is used as the invoice default markup percentage.  
* If multiple lines have the same number of matches then the one with the most recent start date is used.  
* If multiple lines have the same number of matches and the same start date (or none at all) then the line with the lowest line number is used.

For more information, read about [setting up](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_rate_tables) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_Rate table credit card lines

* If multiple lines have the same number of matches then the one with the most recent start date is used.  
* If multiple lines have the same number of matches and the same start date (or none at all) then the line with the lowest line number is used.

For more information, read about [setting up](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_rate_tables) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_Rate table employee expense lines
tags.description:
Rate table employee expense lines contain criteria for applying a default markup percentage to matching employee expense transactions during invoicing. They are owned objects of a rate table object. * If multiple lines have the same number of matches then the one with the most recent start date is used.  
* If multiple lines have the same number of matches and the same start date (or none at all) then the line with the lowest line number is used.

For more information, read about [setting up](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_rate_tables) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_Rate table journal lines
tags.description:
Construction rate table journal lines contain criteria for applying a default markup percentage to matching general ledger transactions during invoicing. They are owned objects of a rate table object. You create, update, and delete journal line objects through operations on the owning rate table.

* Lines with the most matches is used as the invoice default markup percentage.  
* If multiple lines have the same number of matches then the one with the most recent start date is used.  
* If multiple lines have the same number of matches and the same start date (or none at all) then the line with the lowest line number is used.

For more information, read about [setting up](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_rate_tables) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_Rate table purchasing lines
tags.description:
Construction rate table purchasing lines contain criteria for applying a default markup percentage or unit price to matching purchasing transactions during invoicing. They are owned objects of a rate table object. You create, update, and delete purchasing line objects through operations on the owning rate table.

* Each line requires only 1 value be provided. 
* Lines with the exact same values (excluding description and markup %) are considered duplicates and are not allowed.

tags.name: Construction_Rate table timesheet lines
tags.description:
Construction rate table timesheet lines contain criteria for applying a default markup percentage or labor rate to matching timesheet transactions during invoicing. They are owned objects of a rate table object. You create, update, and delete timesheet line objects through operations on the owning rate table.

* Each line requires only 1 value be provided. 
* Lines with the exact same values (excluding description and markup %) are considered duplicates and are not allowed. 
* If no value is given for a property then the line matches on any transaction, otherwise it only matches on transactions with that property. 
* Lines with the most matches is used as the invoice default markup percentage.  
* If multiple lines have the same number of matches then the one with the most recent start date is used.  
* If multiple lines have the same number of matches and the same start date (or none at all) then the line with the lowest line number is used.

For more information, read about [setting up](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_rate_tables) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_Project billable expenses
tags.description:
A project billable expense represents a source expense transaction, such as an
employee expense, purchasing invoice, or timesheet entry, that has been made available
for billing on a construction project.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving billable expense details, reviewing billing amounts
and dimensions, or tracking how much of an expense has been billed to a customer.

**Relationships:** Linked to the source expense transaction that generated it, and
associated with a project contract and project contract line when billed under a contract.

**Lifecycle context:** Created when a billable source expense transaction is selected for project billing, and
updated as the expense is included in customer invoices during the project billing process.

For more information, see [Enter billable transactions](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_billable_transactions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_Project expenses
tags.description:
A project expense represents a source expense transaction, such as a bill, employee expense,
timesheet entry, purchasing or order entry document, credit card transaction, or general
ledger journal entry, that is available for selection to be billed on a project.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve source expense transactions available for selection when
generating billable expenses for a project.

**Relationships:** Sourced from AP bills, employee expenses, timesheets, purchasing and order
entry documents, credit card transactions, and general ledger journal entries. Selected project
expenses become project billable expenses.

**Lifecycle context:** Represents the pre-billing stage of a project expense, before it is
selected and converted into a project billable expense for invoicing.

For more information, see [Enter billable transactions](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_billable_transactions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_Project estimates
tags.description: A project estimate enables you to approximate how much a project might cost to complete. You can compare the actual costs against your estimate to determine if the project is progressing as expected.

tags.name: Construction_Project estimate lines
tags.description: Project estimate line is an amount that can be tied to cost types (categories in the work breakdown structure), tasks, items, or other aspects of your project. Project estimate lines can only be added and updated through the owning `project-estimate` object.

tags.name: Construction_Project estimate types
tags.description: Project estimate types categorize project estimates for reporting purposes and for filtering which project estimate entries post to the GL.

tags.name: Construction_Project change orders
tags.description: Project change orders provide project managers or contract administrators at construction companies a mechanism to group several change requests together, for the purpose of presenting them to the customer for approval, and ultimately, for billing.

tags.name: Construction_Change requests
tags.description:
Change Requests provide construction companies a way to keep track of changes to their projects in terms of cost, price and markup.

A change request may consist of one or more lines of changes that are captured using the construction work breakdown structure (Project + Task + Cost Type) along with cost and price information. Information about other dimensions may also be captured when relevant.

In some instances only the cost is captured, when the change is not billed to the customer. 

Sometimes the cost and price on a change request are the same amount, such as when the cost of a change is simply passed on to the customer.

Sometimes, in the early stages of a change request, you may not have all the information at a line item level. In such cases, you may want to create a change request without any line items, and later go back to it to add line item along with cost and/or price information.

Once a change request is approved, the user would want to update the primary estimate of the project by posting the change request. When the primary estimate is posted to GL budgets, those line items generated by the posting of the change request would also be part of the posting of the project estimate to GL budgets.

tags.name: Construction_Change request lines
tags.description: Change request lines describe the specific changes in a change request. Change request lines can only be added, updated, and deleted through the owning change-request object.

tags.name: Construction_Change request types
tags.description: Construction companies can create custom change request types to categorize and organize change request information for reporting purposes. For example, an `internal` change request type might be used for changes that incur costs to the contractor but are not billed to the customer.

tags.name: Construction_Change request statuses
tags.description: Construction companies can create their own user-defined statuses for change requests. A change request status is mapped to a workflow type, which controls whether change request lines post to the primary project estimate. A workflow type of none (the default) prevents change request lines from posting. Other workflow types, such as pending change, approved change, and so forth, result in posting.

tags.name: Construction_Accumulation types
tags.description:
Accumulation types let construction companies report on transaction costs across cost types.

An accumulation type is typically specified at the level of the standard cost type, but it can also be provided when creating an individual cost type.

tags.name: Construction_Employee positions
tags.description:
You can define a set of employee positions and use those positions in timesheets and rate tables to bill employee labor out at different rates, depending on the work that an employee does at various times during the day.

For example, you may want to bill a customer at one rate for the time that an employee spends unloading a truck, but then bill at a different rate when the same employee does work as an electrical apprentice. You can define a set of employee positions to use on [timesheets](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/time/tags/time_timesheets) and in [rate table timesheet entries](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/construction/groups/project-contract-rate-tables/tags/construction_rate-table-timesheet-lines) to accomplish this.

**NOTE**: The `employee-position` object is used for billing labor, and is different from the [position-skill](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/project-and-resource-management/groups/resources/tags/project_and_resource_management_position-skills) object, which is used to track, categorize, and search for resources according to skills and expertise.

tags.name: Construction_Labor classes
tags.description: You can define labor class objects that can be applied to timesheets and used to determine billing rates and markups for employees.

tags.name: Construction_Labor shifts
tags.description: You can define labor shift objects that can be applied to timesheets and used to determine billing rates and markups for employees.

tags.name: Construction_Labor unions
tags.description: You can define labor union objects that can be applied to timesheets and used to determine billing rates and markups for employees.

tags.name: Construction_Advanced retainage steps
tags.description:
An advanced retainage step defines a single threshold in a multi-step advanced retainage
schedule, specifying the retainage percentage and amounts that apply once the associated
purchasing document or project contract reaches that threshold.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve or manage the individual steps of an advanced retainage
schedule applied to a construction document or project contract.

**Relationships:** Each step belongs to either a purchasing document or a project contract,
based on `recordType`.

For more information, see [Configure retainage](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Configure_Retainage) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Construction_AP releasable retainage
tags.description: An AP releasable retainage has information about which records can be released.

tags.name: Construction_AP retainage releases
tags.description: On an AP bill that has retainage, an AP retainage release is used to release that retainage for payment.

tags.name: Construction_AP retainage release lines
tags.description: Line item in an AP retainage release. Create and maintain retainage release lines from the owning [AP retainage release object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/construction/groups/retainage/tags/construction_ap-retainage-releases).

tags.name: Construction_AR releasable retainage
tags.description: An AR releasable retainage has information about which records can be released.

tags.name: Construction_AR retainage releases
tags.description: On an AR invoice that has retainage, an AR retainage release is used to release that retainage for payment.

tags.name: Construction_AR retainage release lines
tags.description: AR retainage release line - detail of the AR retainage release.

tags.name: Construction_Primary document details
tags.description: Provides detailed information about calculated totals related to the primary document, including associated transactions, projects, and items.

tags.name: Construction_Primary document summaries
tags.description: Represents a summary of a primary document in the construction domain, including transaction details, retainage, and associated metadata.

tags.name: Construction_Primary document AP bills
tags.description: Primary document AP bills represent the Accounts Payable bills that are generated when purchasing documents are converted through the construction workflow. They link the AP bill to its originating source document, providing access to invoice totals, retainage amounts, and related transaction information for financial tracking and reporting.

tags.name: Construction_Primary document AP payments
tags.description: Represents detailed information about Accounts Payable payments, including associated amounts, and related metadata for financial tracking and reporting.

tags.name: Construction_Primary document retainage releases
tags.description: Represents detailed information about retainage release bills, including associated transactions, amounts, and related metadata for financial tracking and reporting.

tags.name: Construction_Compliance records
tags.description: A compliance record applies a compliance type to a specified vendor or primary document so that you can track dates, amounts, and documents that show compliance.

tags.name: Construction_Compliance types
tags.description: A compliance type is a specific license, insurance, or other document that you want to track for vendors. You can associate multiple compliance types with one compliance definition. See [Vendor compliance types](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Ab_TOC_compliance_types) in the Sage Intacct Help Center for more information.

tags.name: Construction_Compliance definitions
tags.description: Compliance definitions provide validation rules and notification settings for tracking vendor compliance. See [Vendor compliance definitions](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Ab_TOC_compliance_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center for more information.

tags.name: Construction_Compliance definition associations
tags.description: Associate compliance definitions with one or more object types, such as vendor type, project type, or document type.

tags.name: Construction_Work orders
tags.description:
Work order is an optional [dimension](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Dimensions_overview_basics) that can be used for tagging, filtering, and categorizing data in many areas of Sage Intacct.

A work order represents a unit of service work to be performed and tracked independently in a construction project.

You can create a hierarchy of work orders. To set up a hierarchy, create the parent work order first and then specify the parent work order when adding child work orders.

tags.name: Construction_Work order types
tags.description: The category for the work order service request, such as urgent repair or software installation.

tags.name: Construction_Work order call types
tags.description: A subcategory for a work order service request. For example, preventative maintenance or warranty repair.

tags.name: Construction_Work order states
tags.description: Identifies the current status for a work order service request. For example, in progress, completed, or on hold.

tags.name: Construction_Work order problem codes
tags.description: A subcategory that describes the source of the work order service issue. For example, parts or electrical.

tags.name: Construction_Property leases
tags.description:
A property lease represents a contract between a landlord and a tenant for the rental of a property.
It includes details such as the start and end dates of the lease, the rent amount, and the terms of
the agreement.

**When to use:** Use to track lease terms, dates, and rent details for a rental property.

**Relationships:** Contains tenants and units, and references an entity, project, class, department,
and property lease type, state, business category, and termination reason.

tags.name: Construction_Property lease business categories
tags.description:
A property lease business category represents the different categories of businesses that can be associated with a property lease, such as retail, office, or industrial.

**When to use:** Use to classify property leases by the type of business operating under the lease.

**Relationships:** Can have a parent property lease business category, forming a property lease business category hierarchy. Referenced by the `propertyLeaseBusinessCategory` field on a property lease.

tags.name: Construction_Property lease states
tags.description:
A property lease state represents the different states that a property lease can be in, such as in progress, completed, or on hold.

**When to use:** Use to track the current status of a property lease, such as in progress, completed, or on hold.

**Relationships:** Can have a parent property lease state, forming a property lease state hierarchy. Referenced by the `propertyLeaseState` field on a property lease.

tags.name: Construction_Property lease tenants
tags.description:
A property lease tenant represents the details of a specific tenant within a property lease and associated tenant information.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the tenants assigned to a property lease.

**Relationships:** Owned by a property lease. References a customer record for the tenant.

tags.name: Construction_Property lease termination reasons
tags.description:
A property lease termination reason represents the different reasons for termination that can be associated with a property lease.

**When to use:** Use to track why a property lease was terminated.

**Relationships:** Can have a parent property lease termination reason, forming a property lease termination reason hierarchy. Referenced by the `propertyLeaseTerminationReason` field on a property lease.

tags.name: Construction_Property lease types
tags.description:
A property lease type represents the different types of leases that can be associated with a property.

**When to use:** Use to categorize property leases by type, such as residential or commercial.

**Relationships:** Can have a parent property lease type, forming a property lease type hierarchy. Referenced by the `propertyLeaseType` field on a property lease.

tags.name: Construction_Property lease units
tags.description:
A property lease unit represents the details of a specific unit within a property lease, including move-in date and associated unit information.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the units assigned to a property lease.

**Relationships:** Owned by a property lease. References a location record for the unit.

tags.name: Construction_WIP setups
tags.description:
Use WIP setup to configure accounts used for your WIP schedules, and a reconciliation method for overbilling and underbilling amounts.

You cannot delete a WIP setup object.

tags.name: Construction_WIP setup accounts
tags.description: Set up accounts for the [WIP setup](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/construction/groups/construction-forecasting/tags/construction_wip-setups) object.

tags.name: Construction_WIP projects
tags.description:
Ongoing projects that may be included in a [WIP schedule](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/construction/groups/construction-forecasting/groups/wip-periods/tags/construction_wip-periods), that provide:
- Project manager and CFO forecasts of project costs, profits, and completion percentage
- Actual costs and earned revenue
- Overbilling and underbilling amounts

tags.name: Construction_WIP forecast details
tags.description: Provides details such as cost, estimate, and project manager forecast for a WIP project.

tags.name: Construction_WIP project manager forecasts
tags.description: Project manager forecasts of project costs, profits, and completion percentage.

tags.name: Construction_WIP target projects
tags.description: Use WIP target project to set WIP project settings: `costsCompleteDate`, `billingsCompleteDate`, and `usePrimaryForecast`.

tags.name: Construction_WIP project settings
tags.description: Use WIP project settings to configure WIP schedules.

tags.name: Construction_Calculate WIP projects
tags.description:
Calculates CFO or product manager (PM) forecast values based on the specified requested calculation. 

For example, when you request a calculation for `cfoForecastContractValue`, the service calculates the `cfoForecast.costToComplete`, `cfoForecast.costAtCompletion`, and `cfoForecast.percentComplete` fields based on the `cfoContractValue` and other actual values such as `jobToDateCosts`.

The extended forecast fields such as `costAtCompletionVariance`, `contractVarianceAmount`, `grossProfitPercentOfCost`, and `earnedProfitToDateAmount`, are calculated using only the CFO forecast and the actuals.

tags.name: Construction_WIP periods
tags.description: Use WIP schedule periods to monitor profitability and revenue recognition for ongoing projects. The WIP schedule periods are based on the reporting periods in your entity. See [Work in progress (WIP) management](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Construction/WIP_management/WIP-management.htm) for details.

tags.name: Construction_Preview WIP periods
tags.description: Determine whether a preview of a WIP period is ready to be posted to the GL or contains any problems that must be resolved.

tags.name: Construction_Generate WIP projects
tags.description:
The generate WIP projects service creates [WIP project](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/construction/groups/construction-forecasting/groups/wip-projects/tags/construction_wip-projects) objects based on calculations of the extended forecast.

Actuals are calculated using data from the general ledger cost and revenue, project estimate, and project contract, combined with the CFO forecast from the prior WIP period.

tags.name: Construction_Prior WIP periods
tags.description: Retrieve a list of prior WIP periods.

tags.name: Construction_Refresh WIP projects
tags.description:
Creates a preview of the WIP schedule for a specified list of projects based on the latest project data.

You can only refresh the data for a WIP schedule period in an `unposted` state.

If refreshing the data changes a calculated value for a project that was set as `finalized`, the project is reset to `active`.

tags.name: Construction_WIP period warnings
tags.description: Perform validation to get the errors and warnings for WIP projects in a specified WIP schedule period.

tags.name: Construction_WIP available periods
tags.description: Get a list of available General Ledger [reporting periods](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/general-ledger/tags/general_ledger_reporting-periods).

tags.name: Construction_WIP next periods
tags.description: Retrieve the next available reporting period that follows the specified period end date.

tags.name: Construction_WIP posting histories
tags.description: Provide the posting and reversal activity for a specified WIP period.

tags.name: Construction_Preview WIP postings
tags.description: Generate a GL journal entry preview for posting a WIP schedule period.

tags.name: Construction_Post WIP periods
tags.description: Post a GL journal entry for a WIP schedule period. All projects in the WIP period must be finalized before you can post it. When you post a WIP schedule, the overbilling and underbilling amounts are posted to the accounts specified in [WIP setup](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/construction/groups/construction-forecasting/tags/construction_wip-setups).

tags.name: Construction_Revert WIP postings
tags.description: Revert the journal transactions that were created when the overbilling or underbilling amount was posted.

tags.name: Construction_WIP rollup projects
tags.description: WIP rollup project service

tags.name: Construction_WIP include projects
tags.description: Include projects as entries in a WIP schedule project. See [Include projects in work in progress (WIP) schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=include_projects_in_wip) for details.

tags.name: Construction_WIP exclude projects
tags.description: Exclude from WIP schedules

tags.name: Construction_WIP include in projects
tags.description: If a WIP schedule project is at or below the second level of the project hierarchy, you can set some or all of its subprojects to be included as part of it. The selected projects must be in the same project hierarchy. See [Include projects in work in progress (WIP) schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=include_projects_in_wip) for details.

tags.name: Construction_WIP include with root project
tags.description: If a root project is included in a WIP schedule, you can include some or all of its subprojects as part of it. You can select subprojects from multiple project hierarchies. See [Include projects in work in progress (WIP) schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=include_projects_in_wip) for details.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Contract groups
tags.description:
A contract group is a logical collection of contracts used to drive reporting and analysis, with contracts as the group members. Contract groups can be defined with specific contracts as members or with filters to dynamically include contracts that meet specified conditions. Contract groups can be used to manage related contracts by grouping them together based on shared characteristics, such as contract type, region, or business unit.

For more information, read about [contracts](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_Contracts) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Contract group members
tags.description:
A contract group member represents a contract that belongs to a contract group. Each member is associated with one contract and one contract group, and the member's properties are determined by the associated contract and contract group. The contract group member object provides information about the contract's membership in the group, such as the sort order of the member within the group and details about the associated contract. Update the contract group member in the owning [contract group](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/contracts-and-revenue-management/groups/contract-setup/tags/contracts_and_revenue_management_contract-groups) object.

For more information, read about [contracts](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_Contracts) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Contract types
tags.description:
Use contract types to categorize contracts and then use them to filter reports, batch invoices, and so on. You can create and maintain contract types that are tailored to your specific business. After creating a contract type, you can then apply it to a contract.

For more information, read about [contract types](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Contract_types) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Contracts
tags.description:
A contract represents a customer agreement that defines the products or services that are provided to a specified customer. It can control settings such as renewals and terms, capture compliance information, and record the transaction history for all contract lines and expenses.

For more information, read about [contracts](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Contract_records) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Contract renewal templates
tags.description:
Contract renewal templates define sets of rules and actions that Sage Intacct performs when renewing a contract, for example:

* Specify when to trigger the renewal relative to the contract end date.
* Determine the pricing source for the renewed contract.
* Send an email to the customer notifying them of an upcoming renewal.
* Set the state of the renewed contract (In Progress or Draft).

For more information, read about [Contract Renewal Templates](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Renewal_templates_contracts) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Contract lines
tags.description:
A contract line defines a specific performance obligation within a contract, representing the agreed promise to deliver a product or service to the customer. It serves as the header for one or more schedule lines and contains the key details that drive both billing and revenue recognition. 

When a contract line is created, Sage Intacct automatically generates the billing and revenue schedules based on the data entered.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Contract transaction histories
tags.description:
A contract transaction history represents a record of a financial transaction related to a contract, such as billing, revenue recognition, or adjustments. It captures details about the transaction, including amounts, dates, types, and related entities like contracts and journal entries. Contract transaction histories are essential for tracking the financial performance of contracts and ensuring accurate accounting and reporting.

For more information, read about [transaction histories](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Contract_fbf) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Compliance checklists
tags.description:
Contract compliance checklist tasks are the sign-off details for tasks within a specific compliance checklist, providing an audit trail of completions. Each compliance checklist task documents who completed the task, when it was completed, sign-off status, and any associated comments. Each compliance checklist task is linked to exactly one compliance checklist and one compliance task template.

For more information, read about the [compliance checklist](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Compliance_checklist) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Compliance notes
tags.description:
Contract compliance notes represent observations and comments associated with a compliance checklist, providing additional context and commentary. Notes capture general comments, risks, or follow-up items and they can be marked as public or private.

For more information, read about the [compliance checklist](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Compliance_checklist) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Compliance tasks
tags.description:
Contract compliance tasks are reusable task templates that define what needs to be checked or completed as part of a compliance checklist. Each task contains metadata such as name, description, task number, and status. Compliance tasks can be included in multiple compliance checklists.

For more information, read about the [compliance checklist](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Compliance_checklist) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Billing schedules
tags.description:
A billing schedule shows when a Flat/Fixed amount for a contract line is expected to be invoiced during the contract term. It shows the scheduled billing date and amount to be billed for each potential invoice. For periods that have been invoiced, it shows the date the invoice posted, the exchange rate associated with the invoice date (if applicable), and the document number. Billing schedules are referenced by [contract lines](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/contracts-and-revenue-management/groups/contract-management/tags/contracts_and_revenue_management_contract-lines).

For more information, read about [billing schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_and_Viewing_a_Billing_schedule) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Billing schedule lines
tags.description:
Line items in a billing schedule represent a single billing for a contract line. You create, update, and delete billing schedule line objects through operations on the owning [billing schedule](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/contracts-and-revenue-management/groups/billing/tags/contracts_and_revenue_management_billing-schedules).

For more information, read about [billing schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_and_Viewing_a_Billing_schedule) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Billing templates
tags.description:
A billing template defines the schedule to invoice the flat/fixed amount for a contract line over the contract term. Use billing templates to create non-linear, percent complete, and other types of custom billing schedules.

For more information, read about [billing templates](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Billing_templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Billing template lines
tags.description:
Line items in a contract billing schedule specify the percentages complete at which you want to invoice. You create, update, and delete billing template line objects through operations on the owning [billing template](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/contracts-and-revenue-management/groups/billing/tags/contracts_and_revenue_management_billing-templates).

For more information, read about [billing templates](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Billing_templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Evergreen templates
tags.description:
Evergreen templates define sets of actions Sage Intacct will perform when a recurring billing period on an evergreen contract line ends, for example:

* Determine when to close the contract line for the previous recurring billing period and create the contract line for the next recurring billing period.
* Determine the pricing source for the recurring billing period
* Send an email to the customer notifying them that the recurring billing period is ending and a new one is beginning.

For more information, read about [Evergreen Templates](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Evergreen_templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Contract usage
tags.description: Contract usage objects represents the quantity of a contract line item that a customer used or consumed during a specific time period. Contract usage is used for [committed](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Committed_quantity_usage) and [variable](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Variable_quantity_billing) quantity billing, and [quantity based revenue recognition](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Qty_based_revenue_recognition).

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Revenue schedules
tags.description:
A revenue schedule defines how and when revenue is recognized for a contract line. For termed contracts, the revenue schedule reflects a fixed recognition period, while for evergreen contracts, it supports ongoing recognition without a specific end date. 

For more information, read about [revenue schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_and_Viewing_a_Revenue_schedule) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Revenue schedule lines
tags.description:
A revenue schedule line represents a single entry in a revenue schedule, detailing the amount and timing of revenue recognition for a portion of a contract line. Each schedule line corresponds to a specific posting date and amount, and may be linked to billing schedule lines for multi-element arrangements (MEAs). Create, update, and delete revenue schedule line objects through operations on the owning `revenue-schedule` object.

For more information, read about [revenue schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_and_Viewing_a_Revenue_schedule) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Revenue templates
tags.description:
A revenue template defines the revenue recognition schedule for the flat/fixed amount associated with a contract line. You can create any number of revenue templates and reuse them across contracts.

For more information, read about [revenue templates](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Contract_revenue_templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_MEA allocations
tags.description:
A multiple-element arrangement (MEA) allocation represents the allocation of revenue to contract lines for a specific MEA allocation, which is used to adjust the revenue recognition schedule for the contract lines included in the MEA allocation. MEA allocations are typically used when there is a change to a contract that requires an adjustment to the revenue recognition schedule, such as adding a new item to the contract or changing the price of an existing item.

For more information, read about [MEA allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_mea_allocations) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Bulk action run summaries
tags.description:
A contract bulk action run summary represents the status of a bulk action request for contract management processing, for example posting or clearing revenue/expense recognition. It contains the results of the request, including the count of records processed successfully and with errors.

For more information, read about [bulk action run summaries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Bulk_action_runs) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Expenses
tags.description:
An expense represents a cost incurred to obtain or fulfill a contract with a customer. The ASC 606 accounting rules require you to amortize contract acquisition expenses over the contract term. The expense object supports termed, evergreen, and kit contract models.

For more information, read about the [expense workflow](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Contract_expense_workflow) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Expense schedules
tags.description:
An expense schedule defines the timing and amounts for expenses related to a contract line. It contains header information and a list of associated expense schedule lines.

For more information, read about [expense schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_and_Viewing_a_Expense_schedule) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Expense schedule lines
tags.description:
An expense schedule line represents a single scheduled expense occurrence for a contract line. It includes details such as the scheduled amount, posting date, and status of the scheduled expense.

For more information, read about [expense schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_and_Viewing_a_Expense_schedule) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Historical schedule runs
tags.description:
A historical schedule run is used to build up reporting balances for historical and in-flight contracts when processing contract schedules in Sage Intacct. Each run will have an as-of date, and will calculate schedule lines up to that date. Once the run is complete, the balances can be used in reports and other API calls that need to know the calculated balance for a contract as of a specific date.

For more information, read about [processing contract schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Process_contract_schedules) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Expense templates
tags.description:
An expense template defines the schedule to recognize an expense amount for a contract or contract line over the contract term. You can create any number of expense templates and reuse them across contracts.

For more information, read about [expense templates](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Expense_templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Expense template lines
tags.description:
An expense template line defines the percentage of the total expense amount to be recognized at a specific number of months from the expense start date. Create, update, and delete expense template lines in the owning [expense template](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/contracts-and-revenue-management/groups/expense-recognition/tags/contracts_and_revenue_management_expense-templates) object.

For more information, read about [expense templates](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Expense_templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Billing price lists
tags.description:
Use billing price lists to create pricing strategies for items with prices that are determined based on a fixed fee, the quantity used, or the contracted quantity. Billing price lists support several pricing models, including prices per thousands, discount tiers, and minimum flat fees. A company can have multiple billing price lists.

For more information, read about [billing price lists](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Billing_price_lists) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Billing price list entries
tags.description:
A billing price list entry contains the pricing for a single item within a specified billing price list. A contract specifies a billing price list, and items from contract lines are priced according to the associated price list.

For more information, read about [billing price list entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Billing_price_list_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Billing price list entry lines
tags.description:
Billing price list entry lines define pricing details for an item specified in a billing price list entry. Details include the starting date for a price, the flat amount, and usage rates. Create and maintain billing price list entry lines from the owning [billing price list entry](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/contracts-and-revenue-management/groups/price-lists/tags/contracts_and_revenue_management_billing-price-list-entries) object.

For more information, read about [billing price list entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Billing_price_list_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_Billing price list entry line tiers
tags.x-displayName: Billing price list entry line tiers
tags.description:
A billing price list entry line tier defines the starting quantity and price for a single tier in a billing price list entry line. Create and maintain billing price list entry line tiers from the owning [billing price list entry line](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/contracts-and-revenue-management/groups/price-lists/tags/contracts_and_revenue_management_billing-price-list-entry-lines) object.

For more information, read about [billing price list entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Billing_price_list_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_MEA price lists
tags.description:
MEA price lists contain standalone selling prices for items sold in multiple-element arrangements. A company that provides multiple products and/or services to customers as part of a single arrangement needs to create one or more MEA price lists. A contract that contains multiple-element arrangements can be linked to an MEA price list.

For more information, read about [MEA price lists](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=MEA_price_lists) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_MEA price list entries
tags.description:
MEA price list entries are used in Multi-Element Arrangements (MEAs) to define fair value pricing for individual products or services included in the arrangement.

For more information, read about [MEA price list entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=MEA_price_list_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_MEA price list entry lines
tags.description:
An MEA price list entry line contains the standalone selling price, or fair value price, associated with an item when it's included in a multiple-element arrangement. You can enter a fair value price as an amount, percentage, or as a price range. You can also use a price range with a price entered as an amount.

For more information, read about [MEA price list entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=MEA_price_list_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Contracts_and_Revenue_Management_MEA categories
tags.description:
MEA categories are used in Multi-Element Arrangements (MEAs) to label products or services included in the arrangement to categorize them for fair value allocation.

Sage Intacct uses fair value categories to distinguish products or services included in an MEA that will be used in the algorithm that determines another item's estimated standalone selling price. 

For more information, read about [MEA fair value categories](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=MEA_fair_value_categories) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expenses
tags.description:
An employee expense represents an expense report submitted by an employee, consisting of
individual expense lines for reimbursement of approved out-of-pocket costs related to
their job.

**When to use:** Use when submitting expense reports, retrieving expense report details,
or tracking reimbursement status throughout the approval process.

**Relationships:** Contains employee expense lines, each with its own tax entries, and is
linked to the employee, expense summary, and the AP bill when AP payment is configured
for reimbursement.

**Lifecycle context:** After an employee submits an expense report, it moves through
manager approval. Once approved, the expense report becomes a reimbursement candidate for
the accounting department to process into a pending reimbursement for payment.

For more information, see [Employee expense reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Aa_TOC_staff_expense_reports) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expense lines
tags.description:
An employee expense line represents an individual expense item within an employee expense
report, recording a portion of the report's costs and how it is reimbursed.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve or analyze individual expense entries that make up an
employee expense report.

**Relationships:** Owned by the employee expense and associated with a GL account or
expense type, payment type, and tax entries.

**Lifecycle context:** Created when an employee adds a line to an expense report and
retained as part of the final expense record for reimbursement processing and reporting.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expense tax entries
tags.description:
An employee expense tax entry represents tax information for an employee expense line,
used for VAT/GST-enabled transactions. 

**When to use:** Use to retrieve tax details recorded against an expense line. Create and
maintain tax entries from the owning employee expense line.

**Relationships:** Owned by the employee expense line and associated with a purchasing
tax detail that defines the applicable tax rate.

**Lifecycle context:** Created when a tax amount is applied to an expense line during
line creation, and retained with the line for VAT/GST reporting and audit purposes.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expense summaries
tags.description: Expense summaries are collections of the same type of transactions, grouped together for processing. Expense summaries are referenced by [employee expense](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/expenses/tags/expenses_employee-expenses) objects. For more information, see [Add, edit, or delete expense summaries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_and_Viewing_Expense_Batch_Information) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expense types
tags.description:
Expense types give recognizable names to GL accounts and are applied to line items in expense reports or expense adjustments. Expense types also act to restrict employee access to GL accounts to those defined in the expense types. 

Expense types can be created for expenses such as Mileage, Relocation, Entertainment, and so on. Expense types are the same for all users company wide. Any GL account can be assigned one or more expense types. A specific offsetting account can be assigned to an expense type as well. If no offsetting account is assigned, the default GL Account for Employee Liabilities is used. For more information, see [Expense types](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_expense_types) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expense payment types
tags.description:
Employee expense payment types track how expenses are paid. Expense payment types can be created for both non-reimbursable and reimbursable expenses. The most common use case is to create expense payment types for company credit cards or checks for non-reimbursable expenses. 

Expense payment types are applied to the line items in an employee expense report or an expense adjustment.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expense adjustments
tags.description: Expense adjustments provide a way to correct the balance for an employee who is overpaid or underpaid for an expense.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expense adjustment lines
tags.description: Expense adjustment lines are individual entries in an employee expense adjustment that represent debits or credits payable to an employee.

tags.name: Expenses_Employee expense approval records
tags.description:
An employee expense approval record captures a single approval action taken on an employee expense or expense line, recording the approver, approval stage, and outcome.

**When to use:** Use this endpoint to retrieve the approval history for employee expenses, audit approval decisions, or track the current state of expenses moving through an approval workflow.

**Relationships:** Linked to an employee expense and optionally to an employee expense line. References the user who approved or declined the expense, the designated approver, and the user who submitted the expense for approval.

**Lifecycle context:** Created when an employee expense enters the approval workflow. Each record represents one action in a potentially multi-stage approval process, from submission through final approval or decline.

tags.name: Expenses_Unit rates
tags.description:
When an employee enters a quantity for reimbursement, it's multiplied by the unit rate to
produce the reimbursement amount. An employee start date determines when the unit rate takes
effect. 

The rate applies only to the expense line items that have an expense date on or after the start date. See [Field description, Create expense reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=FBF_create_staff_expense_reports) in the Sage Intacct Help Center for more information.

tags.name: Expenses_Electronic receipts
tags.description: An electronic receipt is a digital version of a receipt that can be used for employee expense reports. Electronic receipts help to streamline the expense reporting process by allowing employees to easily upload and manage receipts.

tags.name: Expenses_Electronic receipt lines
tags.description: Details for an electronic receipt line on an electronic receipt, including individual expenses and their attributes.

tags.name: Expenses_Expenses to approve
tags.description:
An employee creates and submits an expense report, which is routed to the employee's manager for approval. In some cases, approvals are required from multiple users.

After approval, an expense report becomes a reimbursement request, which is processed by accounting.

tags.name: Expenses_Expense lines to approve
tags.description: An employee creates and submits an expense report, which is routed to the employee's manager for approval. The individual line items on the expense report can be approved or declined for reimbursement.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Assets
tags.description:
Assets are resources used in the operations of a business, such as buildings, manufacturing equipment, office equipment, furniture, fixtures, and vehicles.

The asset object holds information about the asset, including the in-service date, asset cost, and dimensions required to post to the GL. These properties are used to automatically generate depreciation schedules. From period to period, post your depreciation schedule entries until the asset is fully depreciated or disposed.

The Fixed Assets Management application supports both depreciable and non-depreciable assets. Assets that are not depreciable do not have depreciation schedules.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Asset classifications
tags.description:
Asset classifications contain information about General Ledger (GL) accounts and depreciation rules.
Use asset classifications to ensure consistent treatment of similar assets.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Depreciation methods
tags.description:
Depreciation methods determine how an asset's depreciation expense is computed into periods over its useful life.

The following depreciation methods are supported: Straight line, Daily, 150% declining balance, 200% declining balance,
Custom declining balance with true-up, and Custom declining balance without true-up.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Asset depreciation rules
tags.description:
Depreciation rules contain information about the depreciation method, convention, and useful life for an asset, which are used to calculate depreciation for an asset.

When you assign a classification to an asset, the classification's depreciation rules are copied over to the asset. You can then create, update, or delete the depreciation rules on the asset to customize them as needed.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Classification depreciation rules
tags.description:
Depreciation rules contain information about the depreciation method, convention, and useful life for an asset.
Depreciation rules in a classification serve as a standard default for how assets in that
classification are treated. However, you can override the depreciation rules at the asset level.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Depreciation schedules
tags.description: Depreciation schedule tracks the loss in value of an asset over the period of its useful life using a specified [depreciation rule](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/fixed-assets-management/tags/fixed_assets_asset-depreciation-rules).

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Depreciation schedule entries
tags.description: Line items in a [depreciation schedule](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/fixed-assets-management/tags/fixed_assets_depreciation-schedules), which denote the amount and posting date of depreciation entries for an asset.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Setups
tags.description: Set up configuration details for the Fixed Assets Management application. Settings apply to all entities.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Setup posting rules
tags.description: Use setup posting rules to identify the journal, useful life term, convention, and so forth, for fixed asset transactions.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Transfer histories
tags.description: Asset transfer history details, which capture the transfer date and dimension details after an asset transfer operation is performed. For more information see [Transfer an asset](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/FixedAssets/Assets/fa-asset-transfer.htm).

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Transfer journal entry maps
tags.description: This object provides information about journal entries created during an asset transfer.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Disposals
tags.description: This object provides details about asset disposal. You can dispose an entire asset, or dispose part of an asset while continuing to depreciate the remaining portion. See [Asset disposal](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_asset_disposal) in the Sage Intacct Help Center for additional information.

tags.name: Fixed_Assets_Disposal depreciation schedule maps
tags.description: This object provides information about depreciation schedules modified during a full or partial asset disposal.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Accounts
tags.description:
A General Ledger account records balance sheet, income statement, or statistical transactions and organizes them by account type within a company's Chart of Accounts.

**When to use:** Use when creating, retrieving, updating, or deleting accounts and when configuring account behavior for transaction posting, tax reporting, reconciliation, or dimensional requirements.

**Relationships:** An account can be associated with another account for closing activity and can be configured for subledger control, tax reporting, and General Ledger matching.

**Lifecycle context:** Accounts are maintained as part of the company's ongoing financial reporting and transaction-posting processes.

For more information, see [Accounts](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_accounts) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account categories
tags.description:
Account categories are high-level classifications for accounts that appear in balance sheets and income statements. Each category has an account type and normal balance and can be used for tracking statistical data. For companies using the QuickStart template, Sage Intacct provides ready-made account groups based on account categories to simplify setup.

**When to use:** Use account categories to retrieve category details and, for companies using a QuickStart template, classify General Ledger accounts while configuring or reviewing a chart of accounts.

**Relationships:** For companies using a QuickStart template, General Ledger accounts can be assigned to account categories, and Sage Intacct uses those categories to provide ready-made account groups.

**Lifecycle context:** Account categories are predefined, read-only classifications. They can be retrieved throughout the lifecycle of the chart of accounts but cannot be created or updated through this API.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account ranges
tags.description:
An account range defines the lower and upper account numbers that determine which GL accounts it includes. Account groups can include account ranges as group members, along with individual named accounts.

**When to use:** Use account ranges to group GL accounts within an account group for reporting and analysis.

**Relationships:** Owned by an account group and defined by starting and ending GL accounts.

**Lifecycle context:** Account ranges are typically created and maintained as part of the configuration of the General Ledger. Changes to account ranges may impact reporting and analysis within the accounting system.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account name entity maps
tags.description:
An account name entity map assigns a location-specific title to a General Ledger account in a multi-entity company.

**When to use:** Use account name entity maps when the same General Ledger account needs different titles for different locations, such as for location-specific financial reporting.

**Relationships:** Each map links a General Ledger account to a location.

**Lifecycle context:** The map is created or updated during multi-entity financial setup to maintain a location-specific title for a General Ledger account.

For more information, see [account titles by entity](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Account_titles_by_entity) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account allocations
tags.description:
An account allocation defines how amounts from a source pool are distributed across dimensions such as departments, locations, projects, or classes. Its definition includes the rationale, source pool, basis, and target entry details.

**When to use:** Use an account allocation to configure how source amounts are distributed, then create an allocation run to generate entries for selected dates.

**Relationships:** Each account allocation includes a source pool, basis, target, and reverse definition. Together, these specify the amounts to allocate, how to distribute them, where to create the entries, and whether allocated amounts remain in the allocation book or are moved to another book using copy and reverse.

**Lifecycle context:** Create and configure the allocation definition before generating allocations. Use an allocation run to generate entries for the desired dates.

For more information, read about [Account (dynamic) allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_allocations) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account allocation groups
tags.description:
An account allocation group organizes account allocations for coordinated processing. Members can be ordered so that prerequisite allocations are processed first.

**When to use:** Use account allocation groups to process several allocations together and control their processing order when allocations depend on one another.

**Relationships:** Each group contains ordered members that reference account allocations.

**Lifecycle context:** Configure whether processing stops after a member fails or skips the failed member and continues.

For more information, see [Account allocation groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=aa_toc_allocation_groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account allocation group members
tags.description:
An account allocation group member links an account allocation to the group that processes it.

**When to use:** Use account allocation group members to retrieve the allocations included in a group.

**Relationships:** Each member belongs to an account allocation group and references the account allocation processed as part of that group. Members can be created and updated only through their owning account allocation group.

For more information, see [Account allocation groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=aa_toc_allocation_groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account allocation runs
tags.description:
An account allocation run records the execution of an account allocation or account allocation group, including its processing status and any associated journal entry.

**When to use:** Use to execute an account allocation or group, or to check its processing status and associated journal entry.

**Relationships:** A run refers to the allocation or allocation group it executes. It may also reference a parent run, a recurring allocation, and a journal entry generated during processing.

**Lifecycle context:** Runs track execution through queued and in-progress states and record a successful, failed, or partial-success outcome when processing finishes.

For more information, see [Generating allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Generate_account_allocations) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account allocation sources
tags.description:
An account allocation source defines the account group and criteria Intacct uses to identify source amounts for an account allocation. Dimension groups or dimension values can narrow the source pool.

**When to use:** Use an account allocation source to specify the reporting period, account group, percentage to allocate, and reporting-book settings for calculating source amounts.

**Relationships:** An account allocation source belongs to an account allocation and references the account group and reporting period used to select source amounts. It can also include adjustment books and dimension filters.

**Lifecycle context:** Configured as part of an account allocation, the source is used when the allocation runs to determine the amounts available for allocation.

For more information, read about [Account (dynamic) allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_allocations) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account allocation basis
tags.description:
An account allocation basis defines the account activity or balances used to calculate splits for a dynamic account allocation.

**When to use:** Use when configuring a dynamic account allocation to select the account group, reporting period, and accounting rules used to calculate allocation splits.

**Relationships:** Owned by an account allocation, with associated basis adjustment books. It references an account group, reporting period, and the dimension groups or dimension values used to determine basis amounts.

**Lifecycle context:** Created through its owning account allocation rather than directly — this endpoint supports retrieving and updating an existing basis. The basis is evaluated when the allocation runs, to determine how the source pool is distributed.

For more information, see [Create an account allocation definition](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Account_allocations_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account allocation targets
tags.description:
An account allocation target specifies where amounts from the source pool are distributed when a dynamic account allocation is generated.

**When to use:** Use when configuring an account allocation to choose the GL account, journal, and dimension overrides for generated amounts. For allocations that cross entities, set the exchange rate type here.

**Relationships:** Owned by an account allocation and associated with an account group. It can also reference a GL account, journal, and dimensions used as target overrides.

**Lifecycle context:** Created through its owning account allocation rather than directly — this endpoint supports retrieving and updating an existing target. These settings determine the account, journal, and dimensions used on the entries generated each time the allocation runs.

For more information, see [Account (dynamic) allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_allocations) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account allocation reversals
tags.description:
An account allocation reversal defines the account and dimension values used on the offsetting entries for a dynamic account allocation.

**When to use:** Use to set the account and dimension values applied to the reversing source pool entries. You can reuse the accounts from the source pool account group, or nominate a separate reversal account.

**Relationships:** Owned by an account allocation. References the GL account used for the reversal and any dimension overrides applied to the reversing entries.

**Lifecycle context:** Created through its owning account allocation rather than directly — this endpoint supports retrieving and updating an existing reversal. These settings are applied to the reversing source pool entries each time the allocation generates.

For more information, see [Account (dynamic) allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_allocations) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Recurring account allocations
tags.description:
A recurring account allocation schedules an account allocation, or an account allocation group, to run automatically at defined intervals.

**When to use:** Use to set up and maintain automated allocation schedules, and to monitor scheduled runs — the next and last run dates, the most recent execution status, and how many times the schedule has run.

**Relationships:** References either an account allocation or an account allocation group, along with the entity it belongs to. Links to the scheduled operation and the processing operation that carry out each run. Timing settings are held in an embedded schedule.

**Lifecycle context:** Once saved, the schedule repeats at the configured interval, generating allocation journal entries on each run. When `allocateToPeriodEnd` is `true`, the first scheduled run occurs at the start of the next period, with journal entries dated at the preceding period end. It continues until it reaches its end date, completes its set number of occurrences, or is stopped.

For more information, see [Schedule recurring allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Account_allocations_recurring) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account groups
tags.description:
An account group organizes General Ledger accounts into reusable structures that define the accounting data and totals shown in financial reports.

**When to use:** Use account groups to select accounting data for financial reports, graphs, and dashboard performance cards. Create hierarchical structures such as Net Income or flat groups such as Cash and Cash Equivalents.

**Relationships:** Account groups can contain account ranges, accounts, other account groups, category members, or computation members. They can also be associated with an account group purpose and dimension filters.

**Lifecycle context:** Account groups are created, updated, and deleted as part of the financial reporting setup and maintenance process.

For more information, see [Account groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_account_groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account group purposes
tags.description:
An account group purpose classifies account groups according to their intended use, which helps organize financial reporting.

**When to use:** Use when creating, retrieving, updating, or deleting classifications that identify why account groups are used in financial reporting.

**Relationships:** Assigned to account groups when the groups are created or updated.

**Lifecycle context:** Created before they are assigned to account groups and retained as reference data for reporting.

For more information, see [About the account group purpose](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_acct_group_purpose) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account group members
tags.description:
An account group member represents an account group owned by another account group. The owned account group can contain member accounts or other account groups. Account groups can organize individual GL accounts or statistical accounts at the first level, and can contain other account groups to build a hierarchy.

**When to use:** Use when retrieving or analyzing the account groups that make up a hierarchical account group, including their order within the owning group.

**Relationships:** Owned by an account group and references the included account group. The included account group can contain member accounts or other account groups.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as part of an owning account group and remains available until the relationship is removed or the owning account group is deleted.

For more information, see [Introduction to account groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Introducing_account_groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account group category members
tags.description:
An account group category member associates a reporting category with an account group.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve the reporting categories assigned to an account group.

**Relationships:** Owned by an account group and linked to a reporting category.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as part of an account group and remains available until the relationship is removed or the account group is deleted.

For more information, see [Introduction to account groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Introducing_account_groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Computation account groups
tags.description:
A computation account group defines a mathematical formula using other account groups, individual General Ledger accounts, or constants. The calculated result appears in financial reports.

**When to use:** Use computation account groups to calculate values for financial reports from account groups, account balances, or constants.

**Relationships:** Owned by a General Ledger account group and can reference other account groups and General Ledger accounts as formula operands.

For more information, see [Row computations for financial reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=HDI_Add_computation_to_rows) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account group maps
tags.description:
An account group map identifies a General Ledger account and, when applicable, its associated account group in the chart of accounts.

**When to use:** Use account group maps to review account assignments and analyze or report on account groupings.

**Relationships:** Each map identifies one General Ledger account and may include an associated account group when the account matches a group range. Accounts without a matching group range are also returned with no associated account group.

**Lifecycle context:** Referenced during financial reporting to identify any account group associated with each General Ledger account.

For more information, see [Map accounts to account groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Mapping_of_accounts_to_account_groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account group hierarchies
tags.description:
An account group hierarchy defines the parent-child structure of General Ledger (GL) account groups and accounts within the chart of accounts.

**When to use:** Use to review the structure of account group membership, trace how GL account groups and GL accounts are organized, and understand reporting context for account analysis.

**Relationships:** Linked to GL account groups and GL accounts, with optional location and location group context for reporting dimensions.
