**Lifecycle context:** Used as a reference structure in the GL reporting lifecycle to organize account content before reporting or analysis.

For more information, see [organize account groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Organize_account_groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Accounting sequences
tags.description:
An accounting sequence assigns a unique sequential number to each posted transaction that affects the General Ledger (GL).

**When to use:** Use to identify the sequence in which posted GL-impacting transactions are processed for reporting, reconciliation, and audit purposes.

**Relationships:** Linked to accounting sequence lines and associated with the entity and journal records that use the numbering sequence.

**Lifecycle context:** Created to establish the valid date range and numbering sequence for posted transactions within a given entity.

For more information, see [Accounting sequences](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_accounting_sequence) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Accounting sequence lines
tags.description:
An accounting sequence line links a General Ledger journal and a document sequence to an accounting sequence used to number posted transactions.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve and review the journal and document-sequence assignments for an accounting sequence.

**Relationships:** Owned by an accounting sequence and linked to a General Ledger journal and a document sequence.

**Lifecycle context:** Defines the numbering sequence applied to posted transactions for the associated journal.

For more information, see [Accounting sequences](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_accounting_sequence) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Budgets
tags.description:
A budget helps track company performance over time by comparing actual results with forecasted figures across predefined reporting periods. It contains budget detail lines with amounts for General Ledger accounts and reporting periods, which may also include dimensions such as locations, departments, or employees.

**When to use:** Use budgets to plan and track company performance over time by comparing actual results with forecasted figures.

**Relationships:** A budget contains budget details. Each detail is associated with a General Ledger account and reporting period and may include dimensions.

**Lifecycle context:** Create budgets with the API and manage their details as lines on the owning budget. When creating a budget, provide an amount for each budget detail; the API does not calculate amounts for calculated budgets. To update an existing detail, include its `key`; to add a detail, omit its `key`. You cannot delete the default budget or a budget used by a financial report.

Before you create a budget, reporting periods must exist and be marked as available for budgeting. Accounts and dimensions referenced in the budget must already be set up in Sage Intacct.

For more information, see [Before you create a budget](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Planning_Your_Intacct_Budgets) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Budget details
tags.description:
A budget detail records a budgeted amount for a General Ledger account and reporting period, optionally with dimensions such as departments and locations.

**When to use:** Use budget details to retrieve or analyze planned amounts by reporting period, account, and dimension.

**Relationships:** A budget detail belongs to an owning budget and is associated with a General Ledger account and reporting period. It can also include dimensions, including user-defined dimensions. Once saved, its account and dimensions cannot be changed.

**Lifecycle context:** Create and maintain budget details through the owning budget. To track budget data by dimension, create a separate budget detail for each account, reporting period, and dimension combination. For example, to budget travel expenses across three locations, create one budget detail for each location.

For more information, see [Overview of creating budgets](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Creating_Editing_Viewing_Budgets) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Journals
tags.description:
A General Ledger journal categorizes transactions entered directly in the General Ledger or posted from subledgers such as Accounts Payable.

**When to use:** Use journals to organize journal entry activity and identify where General Ledger or subledger transactions are posted.

**Relationships:** Journal entries use a journal. Subledger applications can be configured to post transactions to journals.

**Lifecycle context:** Create a journal before it is used for journal entry activity or configured for subledger posting. You can update journal settings through the API. You can delete a journal only if it has no transactions, and deleted journals cannot be recovered.

For more information, see [What journals do you need?](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Viewing_and_Managing_Journals) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_User-defined books
tags.description:
A user-defined book supports reporting needs beyond standard GAAP and tax books. A book configured for management reporting does not affect actual books and can be included alongside them in reports.

**When to use:** Use user-defined books to support specialized accounting or reporting needs.

**Relationships:** User-defined journals can post only to books configured for management reporting. Subledger applications such as Accounts Payable cannot post to management reporting books.

**Lifecycle context:** Enable user-defined books in the General Ledger before creating one. Choose whether a book is for management reporting when you create it; this setting cannot be changed later. You cannot delete a user-defined book while it is in use.

For more information, see [User-defined books](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_user_defined_books_setup) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_User-defined journals
tags.description:
A user-defined journal is used to create journal entries in a user-defined book.

**When to use:** Use user-defined journals to record entries in user-defined books.

**Relationships:** Each user-defined journal is associated with a user-defined book. User-defined journals can post only to books configured for management reporting.

**Lifecycle context:** Create a user-defined journal before creating entries for its book. If direct posting is disabled, entries must be posted through subledger journals. You can delete a user-defined journal only if it has no transactions.

For more information, see [Entries for user-defined books](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_user_defined_books) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Journal entries
tags.description:
A journal entry records accounting transactions in the General Ledger using debit and credit lines. Debits and credits must balance before the entry can be posted.

**When to use:** Use to record and review manual journal activity, including saving entries as drafts before posting to the General Ledger.

**Relationships:** Contains journal entry lines with account, currency, and dimension details. A journal entry is associated with a journal and can include an entity, base location, tax details, an allocation, or a supporting document.

**Lifecycle context:** A journal entry can be posted or saved as a `draft` for review. Draft entries can be updated before posting. Reversal details are available for entries that have been reversed. The journal entry can also have `submitted`, `partiallyApproved`, `approved`, `declined`, `reversalPending`, or `reversed` states.

When General Ledger Outlier Detection is enabled, Sage Intacct identifies journal entries and allocation splits that deviate from expected patterns. Outlier details are included when retrieving a journal entry.

For more information, see [Journal entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_journal_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Journal entry lines
tags.description:
A journal entry line represents an individual debit or credit entry within a journal entry.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve or analyze line-level account, amount, currency, dimension, and tax details. Create and update lines through the owning journal entry.

**Relationships:** Owned by a journal entry and associated with a GL account. A line can also include dimensions, currency, an allocation, and tax entries.

**Lifecycle context:** Lines are created or updated through the owning journal entry. The line API supports retrieving or deleting an individual line.

For more information, see [Journal entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_journal_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Journal entry tax entries
tags.description:
A journal entry tax entry records tax amounts and tax detail for a journal entry line.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve tax amounts and tax details recorded for VAT/GST-enabled journal entry lines.

**Relationships:** Owned by a journal entry line and associated with a tax detail. Multiple tax entries per line are supported when multiple taxes are enabled in the VAT/GST application configuration.

**Lifecycle context:** Tax entries are recorded with the owning journal entry line. Create, update, or delete them through the parent journal entry request, subject to the VAT/GST configuration and tax solution rules.

For more information, see [Capture tax in a journal entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=capture_tax_in_journal_entry) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Journal entry transaction templates
tags.description:
A journal entry transaction template stores reusable details for creating common journal transactions without requiring users to remember the GL journal and debit and credit accounts.

**When to use:** Use to create common journal entries from saved journal and line details.

**Relationships:** Associated with a GL journal and an optional offset GL account, and contains one or more journal entry transaction template lines.

**Lifecycle context:** A journal entry transaction template remains active until it is explicitly deactivated or deleted. Changes to the template do not affect previously created journal entries.

For more information, see [Transaction templates for journal entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Creating_Editing_and_Viewing_Transaction_Templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Journal entry transaction template lines
tags.description:
A journal entry transaction template line defines a debit or credit entry and its account and dimension settings within a journal entry transaction template.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve or delete an individual line, or to define line details when creating or updating its parent template.

**Relationships:** Owned by a journal entry transaction template and associated with a GL account and dimension values.

**Lifecycle context:** Create lines through POST or PATCH on the parent journal entry transaction template, and update lines through PATCH. Delete a line through this endpoint; the parent template must retain at least one line.

For more information, see [Transaction templates for journal entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Creating_Editing_and_Viewing_Transaction_Templates) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Recurring journal entries
tags.description:
Recurring journal entries automate the creation and posting of journal transactions according to a defined schedule, with optional automatic reversals.

**When to use:** Use when you need to create, retrieve, or manage journal transactions that recur on a regular schedule.

**Relationships:** Contains recurring journal entry lines and can reference a journal, attachment, location, entity, and reversal schedule.

**Lifecycle context:** Defines the schedule and posting details for recurring journal transactions, including optional automatic reversals.

For more information, see [recurring journal entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_reucrring_journal_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Recurring journal entry lines
tags.description:
A recurring journal entry line represents a single debit or credit entry within a recurring journal entry and captures the amount, account, dimensions, and related details for that line.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve, review, or update the individual lines that make up a recurring journal entry.

**Relationships:** Owned by the recurring journal entry and linked to the GL account, currency, and associated dimensions or allocation template.

**Lifecycle context:** Created as part of the recurring journal entry schedule and retained for tracking and posting activity across recurring cycles.

For more information, see [recurring journal entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_reucrring_journal_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Reporting periods
tags.description:
A reporting period defines a date range used to organize financial activity in reports, budgets, and book-close processes.

**When to use:** Use reporting periods to filter financial reports, assign periods to budgets, and manage book opening and closing.

**Relationships:** Budgets and General Ledger reports use reporting periods to associate financial activity with a defined date range.

**Lifecycle context:** Reporting periods are created and managed as part of the financial close process, ensuring that financial activity is accurately captured within the appropriate time frames.

For more information, see [Learn about reporting periods](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Reporting_periods_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Adjustment journals
tags.description:
A general ledger adjustment journal represents journal entries used to make adjustments to closed accounting periods. Each adjustment journal contains its own line items, and you can create as many adjustment journals as needed.

**When to use:** Use when creating, retrieving, or managing journal entries that adjust closed accounting periods.

**Relationships:** Contains its own line items and can be configured to allow or disallow direct posting.

**Lifecycle context:** Used to record adjustments after an accounting period has closed.

For more information, see [Adjustment journals](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Viewing_and_Managing_Adjustment_Journals) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_GAAP adjustment journals
tags.description:
A GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) adjustment journal represents journal entries used to post adjustments without changing historical monthly amounts, maintaining the integrity of operational reporting.

**When to use:** Use when creating, retrieving, or managing adjustments that do not change historical monthly amounts.

**Relationships:** Contains its own line items and can be configured for billable entries and direct-posting behavior.

**Lifecycle context:** Used to record GAAP adjustments while preserving historical operational reporting.

For more information, see [GAAP adjustments](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_gaap_and_tax_adjustments) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Tax adjustment journals
tags.description:
A tax adjustment journal records tax changes for transactions already posted to the general ledger. It helps correct errors, reflect tax law updates, and keep tax liability records accurate and compliant.

**When to use:** Use when creating, retrieving, or managing tax adjustments for transactions that are already posted to the general ledger.

**Relationships:** Contains its own line items and is associated with the general ledger transactions being adjusted.

**Lifecycle context:** Used to correct or update tax information after the related transaction has been posted.

For more information, see [tax adjustments](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_gaap_and_tax_adjustments) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Statistical accounts
tags.description:
A statistical account tracks non-financial quantities in the General Ledger, such as employee headcount, membership, or room counts.

**When to use:** Use statistical accounts to record and report non-financial quantities alongside financial account activity.

**Relationships:** Statistical accounts can be included in statistical account groups and assigned to categories for reporting. In consolidated company structures, they can be consolidated similarly to General Ledger accounts.

**Lifecycle context:** The account can be active or inactive. Accounts used in a book transaction cannot be deleted.

For more information, see [Statistical accounts](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_and_Viewing_Statistical_Account_Info) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Statistical journals
tags.description:
A statistical journal records non-monetary journal entries that increase or decrease values without debits or credits.

**When to use:** Use this endpoint to list, create, retrieve, update, or delete statistical journals referenced by statistical journal entries.

**Relationships:** A statistical journal is referenced by each statistical journal entry recorded in it.

**Lifecycle context:** Create a statistical journal before recording entries in it. You can delete it only when it contains no transactions.

For more information, see [Statistical journals](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_stat_journals) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Statistical journal entries
tags.description:
A statistical journal entry records non-financial transactions in a statistical journal for reporting and analysis.

**When to use:** Use statistical journal entries to record, update, or reverse statistical transactions, or to report on non-financial measures alongside financial activity.

**Relationships:** Each entry belongs to a statistical journal and contains at least one statistical transaction line. A reversed entry links to the statistical journal entry that reversed it.

**Lifecycle context:** Create an entry as a draft for review or post it immediately. Draft entries can be updated before posting, and entries can be reversed.

For more information, see [Statistical journals and journal entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_statistical_journals_and_journal_entries) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Statistical journal entry lines
tags.description:
A statistical journal entry line records an individual non-monetary transaction within a statistical journal entry.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve or analyze the entries that make up a statistical journal entry.

**Relationships:** Owned by a statistical journal entry. Create or update lines by modifying their parent statistical journal entry.

**Lifecycle context:** A line’s lifecycle is managed through its parent statistical journal entry. Create or update lines by modifying the parent entry; lines are posted or saved as drafts as part of that entry.

For more information, see [Create a statistical journal entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Create_stat_JE_1) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Statistical adjustment journals
tags.description:
A statistical adjustment journal stores entries made to closed periods, allowing necessary adjustments without reopening the period.

**When to use:** Use to set up one or more statistical adjustment journals before creating statistical adjusting entries.

**Relationships:** Statistical adjusting entries are posted against this journal to record non-financial adjustments to a closed period.

**Lifecycle context:** Statistical adjustment journals let you record non-financial adjustments to a period after it has been closed, without reopening the period itself.

For more information, see [Add a statistical adjustment journal](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Stat_Adj_Jrnl_Info) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Transaction allocation templates
tags.description:
A transaction allocation template stores reusable allocation lines for distributing a transaction line amount across dimensions. Set `allocateBy` to `percentage` to allocate by percentages, `exactAmount` to allocate specified amounts, or `fixedAmount` to combine exact amounts and percentages. For `fixedAmount`, exact amounts are allocated first, and percentages distribute the remainder.

**When to use:** Apply a template during transaction entry to distribute an amount for one transaction line. You can reuse the template on other lines.

**Relationships:** A template contains lines. Each line specifies an amount or percentage and the dimensions for that allocation, such as department, location, project, or class.

**Lifecycle context:** Transaction allocations are applied to transaction lines during entry and can use standard allocation dimensions. Allocations based on current source balances and allocation bases are handled separately as dynamic allocations.

For more information, see [About transaction allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Allocations_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Transaction allocation template lines
tags.description:
A transaction allocation template line defines an amount or percentage allocated by a transaction allocation template.

**When to use:** Use to retrieve allocation details or review how a transaction allocation template distributes values across dimensions.

**Relationships:** Owned by a transaction allocation template and associated with the dimensions used for allocation.

**Lifecycle context:** Added, updated, and deleted through the owning transaction allocation template.

For more information, see [About transaction allocations](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Allocations_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Financial graphs
tags.description:
A financial graph is a saved visualization of General Ledger data for reviewing financial performance and trends.

**When to use:** Retrieve saved graphs to review financial results or monitor trends.

**Relationships:** A graph's configured data series determine the General Ledger data it displays.

**Lifecycle context:** Financial graphs can be retrieved or deleted. Their details can include a chart type, primary and secondary data series, and an as-of date.

For more information, see [Financial graphs](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_financial_graphs) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Reporting accounts
tags.description:
A reporting account provides an optional reporting structure in the General Ledger. It represents a financial or statistical reporting account and can be linked to one or more General Ledger or statistical accounts.

**When to use:** Use reporting accounts to organize General Ledger accounts into custom groupings for financial reporting, or to organize statistical accounts for reporting quantities or units.

**Relationships:** Each reporting account belongs to one reporting account set and can have reporting account maps that link it to General Ledger accounts for financial reporting or statistical accounts for statistical reporting.

**Lifecycle context:** Created and maintained as part of reporting account set configuration, then used with its account mappings when generating financial or statistical reports.

For more information, see [Reporting accounts](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Reporting_accounts) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Reporting account maps
tags.description:
A reporting account map associates one reporting account with either one General Ledger account for financial reporting or one statistical account for statistical reporting.

**When to use:** Use reporting account maps to define which General Ledger or statistical accounts contribute to a reporting account in custom financial or statistical reports.

**Relationships:** Each reporting account map belongs to one reporting account and links to either one General Ledger account or one statistical account, but not both.

**Lifecycle context:** Created and maintained as part of reporting account setup, then used when generating financial or statistical reports.

For more information, see [Mapping GL accounts to reporting accounts](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Options_for_mapping_reporting_accounts) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Reporting account sets
tags.description:
A reporting account set groups reporting accounts for General Ledger financial and statistical reporting.

**When to use:** Use reporting account sets to organize reporting accounts for financial statements, statistical reporting, or consolidated reporting across entities.

**Relationships:** Each reporting account set has an administrator, contains reporting accounts, and includes permissions that control access for users or user groups.

**Lifecycle context:** Created and maintained during reporting setup. The administrator manages the reporting accounts, account mappings, and permissions associated with the set, which is then used for financial or statistical reporting.

For more information, see [Reporting account sets](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Reporting_account_sets) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Reporting account set permissions
tags.description:
A reporting account set permission defines whether access to a reporting account set is allowed or denied for everyone, a specific user group, or an individual user.

**When to use:** Use reporting account set permissions to control access to reporting account sets for all users, a user group, or an individual user.

**Relationships:** Each permission belongs to one reporting account set and applies either to everyone, a specific user group, or an individual user. The permission specifies whether access is allowed or denied.

**Lifecycle context:** Configured as part of reporting account set security and evaluated when users access the associated reporting account set.

For more information, see [Reporting account sets](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Reporting_account_sets) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Report audiences
tags.description:
A report audience identifies the intended users or stakeholders for a General Ledger report, such as directors, board members, or internal users.

**When to use:** Use report audiences to describe the intended readership of reports and organize reports by audience.

**Relationships:** Associated with an entity when reporting is scoped by entity.

**Lifecycle Context:** Created and maintained during report setup, then referenced to document the intended audience for a General Ledger report.

For more information, see [General Ledger reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=GL_reports_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Report types
tags.description:
A report type identifies the business category of a General Ledger report. Common examples include balance sheets, income statements, cash flow reports, and trial balances.

**When to use:** Use report types to classify General Ledger reports and organize reporting definitions.

**Relationships:** Referenced by reporting objects to identify the report category and may be associated with an entity when reporting is scoped by entity.

**Lifecycle context:** Created and maintained during reporting setup, then referenced when configuring and running General Ledger reports.

For more information, see [General Ledger reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=GL_reports_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Reporting categories
tags.description:
A reporting category organizes General Ledger accounts for financial statement reporting or tracks non-financial operational metrics.

**When to use:** Use reporting categories to group accounts by financial statement classification, such as assets, liabilities, equity, income, cost of revenue, and expenses, or to track operational metrics with statistical categories.

**Relationships:** Linked to General Ledger accounts and account groups, and assigned to accounts for presentation in financial statements and operational reporting.

**Lifecycle context:** Used during account setup and ongoing reporting, where the category provides the classification needed for financial statement generation and operational analysis.

For more information, see [QuickStart overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Quickstart_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account balance reports
tags.description:
The account balance report provides a snapshot of account balances for a specified period, showing opening balances, period activity, and closing balances across accounts and dimensions. This endpoint allows you to submit a request to generate the account balance report for processing. The response includes a `reportId` and `href` that can be used to check the processing status of the report.

**When to use:** Run the account balance report for asynchronous processing and retrieve the report status.

**Relationships:** Related to reporting periods, reporting books, GL accounts, and dimensions such as locations, departments, and projects.

**Lifecycle context:** Generated based on the specified parameters, and the response provides information to track the processing status of the report.

For more information, see [Account balances report](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Running_Account_Balances_Reports) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account balance by dimension reports
tags.description:
The account balance by dimension report provides a detailed view of account balances across specified dimensions, such as location, department, and project, for a given period. This endpoint allows you to submit a request to generate the account balance by dimension report for processing. The response includes a `reportId` and `href` that can be used to check the processing status of the report.

**When to use:** Run the account balance by dimension report for asynchronous processing and retrieve the report status.

**Relationships:** Related to reporting periods, reporting books, GL accounts, and dimensions such as locations, departments, and projects.

**Lifecycle context:** Generated based on the specified parameters, and the response provides information to track the processing status of the report.

For more information, see [Dimension balances reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_dim_bal_rpt) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Account group hierarchy reports
tags.description:
The account group hierarchy report provides a structured view of your account groups, their member account groups, and the accounts within those groups. This report is useful for understanding the organization of your accounts and how they roll up into financial statements. The report can be customized with various parameters to filter and format the output according to your needs.

**When to use:** Run the account group hierarchy report for asynchronous processing and retrieve the report status.

**Relationships:** Related to account groups, account categories, reporting account sets, and General Ledger accounts to define the hierarchy.

**Lifecycle context:** Generated based on the specified parameters, and the response provides information to track the processing status of the report.

For more information, see [Account group hierarchy reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_acct_grp_hier_rpt) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_GL details reports
tags.description:
The GL details report provides a comprehensive view of all transactions and activities recorded in the general ledger accounts for a specified period. This endpoint allows you to submit a request to generate the GL details report for processing. The response includes a `reportId` and `href` that can be used to check the processing status of the report.

**When to use:** Run the GL details report for asynchronous processing and retrieve the report status.

**Relationships:** Related to reporting periods, reporting books, GL accounts, and dimensions such as locations and departments.

**Lifecycle context:** Generated based on the specified parameters, and the response provides information to track the processing status of the report.

For more information, see [General Ledger reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_gl_report) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: General_Ledger_Trial balance reports
tags.description:
The trial balance report provides a snapshot of account balances for a specified period, showing opening balances, period activity, and closing balances across accounts and dimensions. This endpoint allows you to submit a request to generate the trial balance report for processing. The response includes a `reportId` and `href` that can be used to check the processing status of the report.

**When to use:** Run the trial balance report for asynchronous processing and retrieve the report status.

**Relationships:** Related to reporting periods, reporting books, GL accounts, and dimensions such as locations and departments.

**Lifecycle context:** Generated based on the specified parameters, and the response provides information to track the processing status of the report.

For more information, see [Trial balance reports](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_trial_bal_rpt) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Aisles
tags.description: An aisle is one of four optional attributes (zone, aisle, row, and bin face) you can assign to a bin to make it easier to find in the warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Bins
tags.description: A bin identifies a specific location within a warehouse where items are or can be stored. Bins make it easier to find items during transaction processing.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Bin faces
tags.description: A bin face is one of four optional attributes (zone, aisle, row, and bin face) you can assign to a bin to make it easier to find within the warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Bin sizes
tags.description: A bin size in an attribute you can assign to a bin to help determine whether the bin is suitable for storing certain items.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory cycles
tags.description: Create and use inventory cycles to keep track of when to take physical inventory.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Cycle counts
tags.description:
Cycle counting is an inventory auditing procedure in which a small amount of inventory is regularly counted in the warehouse. The general goal is to count the entire inventory over a period of time and update the inventory at the end of each count.

An inventory control cycle count object contains high-level information about a cycle count, such as the warehouse where the count is being conducted and the employee that will count the inventory. The lines in a cycle count represent individual items being counted.

For more information, see [Cycle counts overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Cycle_counts_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Cycle count lines
tags.description:
Cycle count lines represent the items included in a cycle count. You can create or update line items by modifying the cycle count.

A cycle count line records the quantity and location of an item included in a cycle count. Each line is associated with a specific cycle count through the `cycleCount` field.

For more information, see [Cycle counts overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Cycle_counts_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory documents
tags.description:
An Inventory Control document contains information about inventory transactions. An inventory transaction is usually an adjustment or a transfer. When you create a new document, it represents the first transaction in a workflow and it can only be converted to the next transaction in a workflow. 

For more information, see [Define transactions](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Create_Inventory_Transaction_Redirect) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory document lines
tags.description: Line information for inventory transactions, including opening balances and adjustments. Create and maintain document lines from the owning [document object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/inventory-control/groups/documents/tags/inventory_control_inventory-documents).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory document line details
tags.description: This object contains warehouse inventory details for all or part of a document line, including serial number, aisle, bin, and row per item.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Document line supplies details
tags.description: This object provides inventory supplies details for document lines.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory document histories
tags.description: An inventory document history contains one entry for each existing transaction in the workflow associated with the selected transaction.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory document subtotals
tags.description: Details of subtotals, taxes, discounts, charges, and more for an inventory transaction.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Supplies documents
tags.description:
A supplies document lists purchasing requisition line items that are enabled for the Supplies workbench. The Supplies workbench helps manage internal supplies that employees need day-to-day, and program-related supplies that support a company's mission or operations. 

For more information, see [Using the Supplies workbench](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=supplies-workbench) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Supplies document details
tags.description: This object provides supplies requisition details for line items listed in a supplies document.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Items
tags.description:
Items are goods, services, or kits that you purchase from vendors or sell to customers. Items are used in Inventory Control, Order Entry, and Purchasing. The type of an item (`itemType`) affects other item parameters. 
Possible item types are:
* `inventory` - Items that will be available in inventory, sales, and purchasing transactions.
* `nonInventory` - Items that will be available in both sales and purchasing transactions or contracts.
* `purchaseOnlyNonInventory` - Items that will only be available in purchasing transactions or contract expenses. 
* `salesOnlyNonInventory` - Items that will only be available in sales transactions or contracts.
* `kit` - The parent item of a (non-stockable) kit (which is assembled from other items at the time of the order). This type is only available if Kits is enabled in either Order Entry or Inventory Control.
* `stockableKit` - The parent item of a stockable kit (which is assembled from other items and stored before order). This type is only available if Stockable kits is enabled in Inventory Control.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item cross references
tags.description:
An item cross reference associates an inventory item with a specific customer or vendor, or with another inventory item.

When an inventory item is associated with a customer or vendor (known as an external cross-reference), the customer or vendor can provide their own identifiers for inventory items that can be used in transactions.

When an inventory item is associated with another inventory item (known as an internal cross-reference), you can provide an alternate item to substitute, upgrade, downgrade, or complement that item in Order Entry transactions in Sage Intacct. For more information, see [Item cross references](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Item_cross_references_OE) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item landed costs
tags.description:
A landed cost item is a non-inventory item that represents a landed cost expense, such as freight, insurance, customs duties, or handling fees.

This object is valid when Inventory Control is configured to enable landed costs.
For more information, see [Landed costs overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Landed_costs_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

Create and maintain landed costs from the owning [item object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/inventory-control/groups/items/tags/inventory_control_items).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item vendors
tags.description: This object provides details about an item that can be purchased from a particular vendor. Create and maintain item vendors from the owning [item object](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/inventory-control/groups/items/tags/inventory_control_items).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item warehouse inventory information
tags.description: Warehouse inventory information is used with Inventory and Stockable Kit items. Sage Intacct uses the information from these records in the Inventory Reorders report.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item warehouse standard costs
tags.description: This object allows you to record different standard costs for different date ranges for item and warehouse combinations.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item warehouse vendors
tags.description: Use this object to specify the vendor information you want to use in the replenishment calculations for the item in this warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item groups
tags.description: An item group categorizes item dimension records, mainly for the purpose of structuring financial reporting.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item GL groups
tags.description: Item GL groups are used to organize transaction definitions for posting to the general ledger.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item warehouse available inventories
tags.description: This object provides information about available quantities for items, including warehouse tracking information.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item tax group item maps
tags.description:
An item tax group item map associates a tax schedule with items and item tax groups, which drive the taxes that are applied to a line item.

Applicable when using Advanced Tax without the Taxes module. For more information see [Tax Schedule Maps](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Tax_schedule_maps).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Kit components
tags.description: Components are items included in a kit. Kits are common combinations of items that can be ordered and invoiced as a single item to simplify data entry. Kits can include inventory items, non-inventory items, and other kits.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Price lists
tags.description: A price list is a container for price list entries. Each associated price list entry should have a unique combination of item or product line, currency, start and end date range, and, optionally, minimum and maximum quantity range. For more information about price lists, see [Price lists - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Price_lists_oe) and [Price lists - Purchasing](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Purchasing_price_list) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Price list entries
tags.description: An inventory price list entry contains the pricing for a selected item within a selected price list. You can create price list entries for items whose prices are determined based on an amount, a discount or mark-up percentage, the quantity sold, and more.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Product lines
tags.description: Product lines are groups of related products. Using product lines makes it easier to update prices and track inventory movement. See [Product lines](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Product_lines_oe) for more information.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Rows
tags.description: A row is one of four optional attributes (zone, aisle, row, and bin face) you can assign to a bin to make it easier to find in the warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Stockable kit documents
tags.description:
Component items in a stockable kit are assembled together to make it an inventoried item. Stockable kit documents provide a record of stockable kit build and disassembly transactions.

When stockable kits are built, the inventory of the components added to the stockable kit is reduced and the number of stockable kits is increased.
When stockable kits are disassembled, the inventory of the components removed from the stockable kit is increased and the number of stockable kits is decreased.

For more information, see [Kits](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_kits) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Stockable kit document lines
tags.description:
Each stockable kit document line object lists the stockable kits that were built or disassembled and the component items that were included in the kits. These transactions are recorded for inventory management and tracking purposes.

You can create or update document line items by creating or modifying the [stockable kit document](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/inventory-control/tags/inventory_control_stockable-kit-documents).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Posting summaries
tags.description:
An inventory control posting summary provides a summary of how an inventory transaction is posted to the general ledger (GL), including the resulting journal entry and related posting information.

**When to use**: Use the posting summary object to retrieve information about a transaction definition after it posts to the general ledger, including the journal entry record number. 

**Relationships**: Posting summaries are derived from inventory transaction definitions and are associated with the resulting general ledger entries generated during posting.

**Lifecycle context**: Posting summaries represent the final accounting outcome of the transaction and persist as part of the audit trail, supporting financial reporting, reconciliation, and traceability between operational inventory activity and financial records.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory totals
tags.description:
Use inventory totals to keep track of the items on hand that are available for sale. Sage Intacct is preconfigured with nine inventory totals for tracking inventory that's damaged, in transit, on hand, on hold, on order, requisitioned, or is scrap and spoilage. You can also create your own inventory totals as needed.

An inventory total can be assigned to a transaction definition so that the specified total is affected when a transaction with that definition template is saved. For more information and a detailed example, see [Inventory totals](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_Viewing_Inventory_Total_Information) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Landed cost categories
tags.description:
Landed cost categories are labels that identify the distribution method for proportionately applying the amount of a landed cost, either estimated costs or actual costs, to the applicable inventory items in the original purchase transactions.

When you create a category, you can specify a distribution method of count, value, volume, or weight. For more information, see [Landed cost categories](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Landed_cost_categories) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Lot categories
tags.description: Lot categories let you group a specific set of items that have something in common. For example, you can create categories for items with similar characteristics, such as perishable goods, chemicals, medical supplies, or health and beauty products.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Replenishment forecasts
tags.description:
When the expected demand for an inventory item fluctuates greatly over time, for example if the item is seasonal, use a replenishment forecast to more accurately predict your inventory needs. During the replenishment process, Sage Intacct uses the replenishment forecast to determine the forecasted demand of the item during the vendor lead times to determine if the item needs reordering.

For more information see, [Replenishment](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_replenishment_setup) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Replenishment forecast lines
tags.description: Line items of the replenishment forecast. Each line item represents the forecasted demand for an item in a warehouse on a specific date. You can create or update line items by modifying the owning replenishment forecast.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Replenishment runs
tags.description:
This object contains details about purchase orders generated by an inventory replenishment run, including whether each requested purchase order was created successfully. 

A replenishment run record is generated each time you create purchase orders using the replenishment process to reorder items. For more information, see [Replenishment runs](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Replenishment_runs) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Replenishment run lines
tags.description: This line object represents the details of a purchase order generated from the owning replenishment run, such as the vendor, number of items, transaction amount, and creation state of the purchase order.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Serial masks
tags.description:
Serial masks define the format for product serial numbers. Serial numbers are strings of alphanumeric characters used to identify particular inventory items.

After creating a serial mask, you then assign the mask to appropriate inventory items. When users enter serial numbers for those items, the system checks that the numbers comply with the mask format. This helps ensure that serial numbers are consistent and valid across your inventory. 

For more information, see [Serial masks](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_Viewing_Serial_Mask_Information) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Valuation maintenance objects
tags.description:
Inventory Control valuation maintenance operations allow you to detect any issues that may exist for your inventory valuation, including current unit costs and cost of goods sold (COGS), and update these costs.

Use the `action` property to specify whether you want to just analyze and report potential issues with your inventory valuation, or also update unit costs and COGS to resolve any issues detected. 

When you create a valuation maintenance object, you can choose to run it immediately or schedule it to run in the future. You can also specify filters to limit the scope of the operation, such as which warehouses, items, or cost methods to include. After the operation runs, you can view the results to see if any issues were detected and what actions were taken.

For more information, see [Schedule Inventory Valuation Maintenance](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Schedule_inventory_valuation_maintenance) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definitions
tags.description: A transaction definition includes the accounting rules, workflow settings, security settings, and other characteristics for a transaction. For more information, see [Transaction Definitions - Inventory Control](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Inventory_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition COGS GL details
tags.x-displayName: Inventory transaction definition COGS GL details
tags.description:
The inventory transaction definition COGS GL detail object defines the general ledger account mappings used when an inventory transaction posts cost of goods sold (COGS) adjustments. It ensures that inventory transactions consistently generate the correct debit and credit entries in the general ledger based on configured rules and dimensions.
**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or retrieve how inventory transactions map to COGS and related GL accounts, particularly for integrations that require accurate financial posting behavior. It is also used when configuring or validating accounting rules tied to inventory transaction definitions.





 **Relationships**: This object is part of inventory transaction definition configuration and works with related objects that define totals, subtotals, sources, and entity settings, collectively determining both the operational and accounting behavior of inventory transactions.

 **Lifecycle context**: This object plays a role in the posting stage of the lifecycle, where processed inventory transactions generate financial entries and update the general ledger with COGS and related account impacts.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition entity details
tags.description:
This object contains entity-specific configuration settings for an inventory transaction definition, including which entities can create transactions and how those transactions are configured at the entity level. These settings are applicable to transaction definitions that are configured to create transactions at the "Top level or entity" or "Entity only" level.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to determine or configure how a transaction definition behaves for specific entities, such as identifying where a definition is available, how transactions are numbered, or which templates are applied within each entity.

**Relationships**: Entity details are associated with an inventory transaction definition, which serves as the template governing the behavior of inventory transactions. They extend the base transaction definition by applying entity-level overrides and configurations in multi-entity companies.

**Lifecycle context**: Entity details are defined as part of transaction definition setup and configuration, particularly in environments using entity-level or top-level transaction creation. They are applied before transactions are created and remain in effect throughout the lifecycle of transactions generated under the definition, influencing document creation, numbering, and presentation at the entity level.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition sources
tags.description:
The inventory transaction definition source object defines how an inventory transaction can originate from other transaction types by specifying the document conversion rules and source relationships within a workflow. It ensures that transactions are created within the correct business context, with relevant data carried forward consistently and traceably.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or retrieve the valid source transactions for an inventory transaction definition, or when supporting document conversion workflows that rely on upstream transaction relationships.

**Relationships**: This object is part of Inventory transaction definition configuration and works with related objects that define entity behavior, totals, subtotals, and accounting impacts, collectively shaping how transactions are created, processed, and posted.

**Lifecycle context**: This object governs the conversion stage of the inventory transaction lifecycle, where upstream transactions are transformed into downstream transactions, ensuring that transitions between workflow stages follow defined and valid paths.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition subtotal details
tags.description:
Inventory transaction definition subtotal detail objects define the subtotal types supported by an inventory transaction definition and help structure how intermediate values are grouped within a transaction. Subtotal configuration shapes how transaction data is organized and presented as part of the overall transaction definition.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or retrieve the subtotal behavior for an inventory transaction definition, especially in integrations that depend on how transaction values are grouped before final totals are calculated. It is also relevant when you are documenting or validating transaction-definition configuration for inventory workflows.

**Relationships**: This object is part of Inventory configuration and works alongside related objects that define sources, totals, entity-level settings, and accounting behavior for the same transaction definition. Together, these objects describe how an inventory transaction is configured, processed, and tracked across the workflow.

**Lifecycle context**: This object plays its primary role during transaction-definition setup, where the structure and calculation behavior of inventory transactions are configured before users enter or process transactions. Its impact carries forward into transaction entry and processing by determining how subtotal information appears within the transaction's overall flow.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition total details
tags.description:
The inventory transaction definition total detail object defines how an inventory transaction affects tracked inventory totals, such as on-hand or on-order quantities. It ensures that each transaction consistently updates inventory balances according to the rules configured in the transaction definition.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or retrieve how a transaction impacts inventory totals or when building integrations that depend on accurate inventory balance updates.

**Relationships**: This object is part of Inventory configuration and works alongside related objects that define sources, subtotals, and accounting behavior to fully control how transactions are processed and recorded.

**Lifecycle context**: This object plays a role in the processing and posting stages of the lifecycle, where inventory transactions update balances and reflect their impact on stock availability and tracking.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Units of measure
tags.description:
Details for a unit of measure included in a unit of measure group. Sage Intacct places related units of measure into groups.
For example, the Count group includes related units of measure such as each, pair, and dozen. For more information, see [About unit of measure groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_uom_groups_oe).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Unit of measure groups
tags.description:
Unit of measure group are provided for items handled under Inventory Control, Order Entry, and Purchasing. Intacct places related units of measure into groups.
For example, the Count group includes related units of each, pair, and dozen. 
The unit of measure (UOM) groups that are provided with Sage Intacct cannot be deleted. Use the Sage Intacct UOM groups as is and create custom UOM groups. 
For more information, see [About unit of measure groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_uom_groups_oe).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Warehouses
tags.description: A warehouse can be an actual warehouse, a store, or any type of stocking location or site that requires inventory tracking and management. Warehouse also serves as a dimension that can be set on transactions to expand report functionality and insight. See [Create warehouses](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Warehouses) for more information.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Warehouse transfers
tags.description:
Use warehouse transfers to transfer items between warehouses or to transfer items between bins in the same warehouse. When you post a warehouse transfer, Sage Intacct creates the underlying system transactions, which includes automatically propagating the costs of the items.

You cannot change the cost of the items when they move into the destination warehouse. For more information, see [Warehouse transfers overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Warehouse_transfer_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Warehouse transfer lines
tags.description: Lines in a warehouse transfer represent items included in the transfer and details about those items. You can create or update warehouse transfer lines by creating or modifying the [warehouse transfer](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/inventory-control/tags/inventory_control_warehouse-transfers).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Warehouse groups
tags.description:
A warehouse group categorizes warehouse dimension records, mainly for the purpose of structuring financial reporting.

For more information, see [About warehouse groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=IC-warehouse-dimension-groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Zones
tags.description: A zone is one of four optional attributes (zone, aisle, row, and bin face) you can assign to a bin to make it easier to find in the warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item activity reports
tags.description:
An Item Activity report contains detailed information about which items are available (on-order, on-hand, and reserved quantity totals), and where they are located. Use the Item Activity report to view:
* Items available in each warehouse.
* Types of item transactions for a selected period.
* Availability of items that are components of a kit (creating a sales order for a kit moves the component items to reserved status).

For more information, see [Item Activity report](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Running_Item_Activity_Reports) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory valuation reports
tags.description:
An Inventory Valuation report displays a list of inventory items, quantities available, item cost, and costing method. The total of all items is the total inventory value on the balance sheet.

The report is divided into two sections: Summary and Detail. The Details section shows what's on the shelf, the summary section shows the value in a warehouse.

For more information, see [Inventory Valuation report](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Running_Inventory_Valuation_Reports) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Documents
tags.description:
An Order Entry document contains information about sales transactions. An order entry transaction can be a quote, order, shipper, invoice, or adjustment. When you create a new document, it represents the first transaction in a workflow, and it can only be converted to the next transaction in a workflow.

See [Transactions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_oe_transactions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center for more information.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Document lines
tags.description: Line items in an Order Entry document represent Order Entry transactions.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Document line details
tags.description:
Inventory tracking details including serial number, aisle, bin, and row per line item.

Create and maintain document line details by creating and updating the `trackingDetail` in the owning [document line objects](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/order-entry/groups/documents/tags/order_entry_document-lines).

tags.name: Order_Entry_Document line subtotals
tags.description: Details of the subtotals, taxes, discounts, charges, and more for the document line.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Document histories
tags.description: An Order Entry document history contains one entry for each existing transaction in the workflow associated with the selected transaction.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Document subtotals
tags.description: Details of subtotals, taxes, discounts, charges, and more for an Order Entry transaction.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Document configuration preferences
tags.description: This object specifies configuration preferences for transaction definitions, including which journals to post to and the email template to use when sending emails from a transaction.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Price lists
tags.description: Order entry price lists contain the sales prices for products or services used in sales transactions. Create a price list and then create the price list entries associated with the list. See [Price lists — Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Price_lists_oe) for more information.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Price list entries
tags.description:
Contains the pricing for a selected item within a selected price list. You can create price list entries for items whose prices are determined based on an amount, a discount or mark-up percentage, the quantity sold, and more.

For more information, see [Price list entries - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Price_list_entries_oe) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Price list entry tiers
tags.description:
A price list entry tier defines a starting quantity and rate for a single pricing band within a tiered billing price list entry.

**When to use:** Use when setting up or reviewing the quantity-based pricing bands that determine the rate applied to transactions within a price list entry.

**Relationships:** Owned by the [price list entry](/intacct/apis/intacct/1/intacct-openapi/groups/order-entry/tags/order_entry_price-list-entries), which defines the tiered pricing that each tier's quantity range and rate apply to.

**Lifecycle context:** Defined during price list setup, before any transactions reference the price list entry. At transaction time, Sage Intacct selects the tier whose quantity range matches the transaction line to determine the applicable rate.

For more information, see [price list entries](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Price_list_entries_oe) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Price schedules
tags.description: Price schedules are pricing groups that you can assign to one or more customers.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Renewal templates
tags.description: Order Entry renewal templates define the structure and rules for automating contract or subscription renewals. When you create a sales transaction from a transaction definition that has renewals enabled, you can select a renewal template to use for a particular transaction line item. To learn more, see [Renewal Templates - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Renewal_templates_OE) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Subtotal templates
tags.description:
Subtotal templates represent a reusable set of subtotal definitions that can be applied to order entry transaction definitions to control how intermediate totals, such as discounts, charges, or taxes, are calculated and displayed within a transaction.

**When to use**: Use this object in multi-entity organizations when you need to standardize or manage how subtotals are calculated in order entry transactions, such as applying consistent discount structures, tax calculations, or grouped totals across different transaction definitions.

**Relationships**: Subtotal templates are referenced by order entry transaction definitions, which use them to determine how subtotals are calculated and presented within transactions. Each template contains one or more subtotal lines that define calculation logic and posting behavior.

**Lifecycle context**: Subtotal templates are created and configured as part of transaction definition setup, particularly in environments using advanced workflows. Once assigned to a transaction definition, they are applied during transaction creation to calculate subtotals, and changes to templates typically affect only new transaction definitions or configurations going forward.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Subtotal template lines
tags.description:
Subtotal template lines represent individual subtotal definitions within a subtotal template, defining how a specific intermediate value, such as a discount, charge, or tax, is calculated, applied, and posted within an order entry transaction. Each subtotal template line specifies the calculation type, default value, application logic, and general ledger (GL) posting behavior for that subtotal.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or manage the calculation logic for individual subtotals within a template, such as configuring discount percentages, freight charges, or tax amounts, and controlling how these values are applied to transaction lines.

**Relationships**: Subtotal template lines are components of a subtotal template, which is referenced by order entry transaction definitions. Each line contributes a single subtotal rule, and multiple lines together define the full set of subtotal calculations applied within a transaction.

**Lifecycle context**: Subtotal template lines are created and maintained as part of subtotal template configuration. When a template is assigned to a transaction definition, its lines are applied during transaction processing to calculate intermediate totals, validate amounts, and generate corresponding GL postings. Changes to template lines typically affect only future configurations or newly created transaction definitions.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Customer GL groups
tags.description: Customer GL groups are categories of customers grouped together so that transactions can be posted to specific GL accounts. Assign each customer record to a customer GL group. Finally, map the customer GL group to GL accounts within transaction definitions.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Recurring documents
tags.description: A recurring document contains the transaction header, line item details, and schedule information that Sage Intacct uses to create recurring transactions. For more information about recurring transactions, see [About recurring transactions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_recurring_transactions_oe) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Recurring document lines
tags.description: Line items in a recurring document represent recurring transactions.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Recurring document subtotals
tags.description: Details of subtotals, taxes, discounts, charges, and more for the transaction.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Recurring schedules
tags.description:
Recurring schedules define how and when a sales transaction (such as an invoice or order) repeats over time. They automate the creation of multiple transactions from a single template, reducing manual effort for recurring billing scenarios. 

Recurring schedules are only used when a user converts a transaction by line item. For more information see, [Recurring schedules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Recurring_schedules_oe) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction definitions
tags.description:
A transaction definition is the template for a sales transaction. It contains the accounting rules, workflow settings, and other configuration settings that determine a transaction's behavior.

See [About transaction definitions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_OE_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center for more information.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction definition additional GL details
tags.description:
Use this object for additional General Ledger account mapping. When additional GL posting is enabled for the owning transaction definition, the `postToGL` field is set to `true`, additional GL posting account mapping is available. 

The item GL group and warehouse together form the criteria set for the account mapping. For more information, see [Transaction definitions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Order_Entry_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Accounts Receivable or direct GL account details
tags.x-displayName: Accounts Receivable or direct GL account details
tags.description:
If the owning Order Entry transaction definition has transaction posting set to either Accounts Receivable or General Ledger (the `txnPostingMethod` field is set to `toAR` or `toGL`), the applicable account mapping is defined using this object.

The item GL group, warehouse, and customer GL group together form the criteria set for the account mapping. For more information, see [Transaction definitions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Order_Entry_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction definition COGS details
tags.description:
This object holds the COGS account and Inventory account mapping for the owning transaction definition. This account mapping is supported if:

 * Your company subscribes to Inventory Control. 
 * Your company does not subscribe to Inventory Control, but `enableCosting` is set to `true` in the owning transaction definition.

The item GL group, warehouse, and customer GL group together form the criteria set for the account mapping. For more information, see [Transaction definitions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Order_Entry_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction definition entity details
tags.description:
The fields in this object are applicable if the owning transaction definition allows transactions to be created from the top level or entity (`topLevelOrEntity`) or entity level only (`entityOnly`). You can use this object to define different settings for each entity.

For more information, see [Transaction definitions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Order_Entry_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction definition inventory total details
tags.description:
Use this object to specify the inventory running total that will be affected by the transaction, whether to track quantity, value, or both, and whether the running total will increase or decrease when the user saves the transaction.

For more information, see [Transaction definitions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Order_Entry_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction definition source document details
tags.description:
Specifies the transaction definition from which the transaction can be converted.

For more information, see [Transaction definitions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Order_Entry_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction definition subtotal details
tags.description:
When `enableSubtotals` in the owning transaction definition is set to `true`, use this object to provide subtotal details for that transaction definition.

For more information, see [Transaction definitions - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Order_Entry_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction buy to order preferences
tags.description:
Buy to order is a workflow that lets you automatically order stock to fill a customer sales order. With buy to order enabled, Sage Intacct allows the system to automatically create purchasing transactions for sales transaction line items that are selected for buy to order. The buy to order items are shipped to you or a third party for final finishing and shipping.

This object specifies the sales transaction definition and purchasing transaction definition that are associated with the buy to order workflow.

For more information, see [Set up a buy to order workflow](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_buy_to_order) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Order_Entry_Transaction drop ship preferences
tags.description:
Drop ship is a workflow that lets you ship orders directly from a vendor to your customer, potentially saving inventory costs. When drop ship is enabled, Sage Intacct automatically creates a purchase transaction with the applicable information when you create a sales transaction and indicate drop ship.

This object specifies the sales transaction definition and purchasing transaction definition that are associated with the drop ship workflow. 

To use drop ship, your company must be subscribed to Order Entry and Purchasing. To learn more, see [Set up a drop-ship workflow](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Set_up_drop_ship) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Project_and_Resource_Management_Projects
tags.description:
Use projects in Sage Intacct to plan, manage, track, and report on work across your organization. Projects provide visibility into activities, costs, and outcomes, helping to ensure accountability and measure performance effectively. The project management capabilities in Sage Intacct enable organizations to streamline their project workflows, improve collaboration, and gain insights into project performance.
